VSD: harsh holosystolic lower-left sternal murmur; ASD: **fixed split S2**, pulmonic flow murmur, RV volume overload
PDA: continuous machinery murmur, bounding pulses; coarctation: weak femoral pulses, arm–leg BP gradient
Central cyanosis: blue lips/tongue, warm extremities → **low arterial saturation**; peripheral: cold extremities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Left-to-right shunts (VSD, ASD, extracardiac PDA) increase pulmonary flow; remodeling can reverse flow → Eisenmenger syndrome
Duct-dependent lesions require pulmonary/systemic flow or mixing through fetal communications
High neonatal PVR limits VSD shunt → murmur appears/louder over weeks as **PVR falls**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Preductal/right-hand and postductal/foot oxygen saturation; **echocardiography** defines anatomy
★ Hyperoxia test: little PaO2 rise with 100% oxygen suggests cardiac shunting; echo preferred
ECG and chest radiograph support diagnosis; normal murmur does not exclude critical disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected duct-dependent lesion → **prostaglandin E1** immediately; monitor for apnea
★ Tet spell (agitation, softer murmur) → knee–chest, oxygen, fluids, morphine; refractory → phenylephrine or propranolol
TGA with inadequate mixing → balloon atrial septostomy, then arterial switch
Large shunts → diuretics, closure; premature PDA → ibuprofen; **obstructed TAPVR → emergency repair**
Coarctation → repair; post-repair paradoxical hypertension → **IV beta-blocker**; Eisenmenger → **do not close shunt**

rows.label: Complications
items: Pulmonary hypertension, failure to thrive, arrhythmias, infective endocarditis
Right-to-left shunting → brain abscess, paradoxical emboli, secondary erythrocytosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Pulse-ox newborn screening; rubella immunization before pregnancy; maternal glycemic control
Endocarditis prophylaxis for selected unrepaired cyanotic or prosthetic-material lesions during dental procedures

rows.label: Mimics
items: Lung disease: substantial oxygen response, pulmonary findings
PPHN: elevated pulmonary resistance with structurally normal heart

table.title: Five cyanotic lesions
rows: RV obstruction, VSD, overriding aorta, RVH; boot-shaped heart
Parallel circuits; single S2; egg-on-string silhouette
Pulmonary veins drain systemically; obstruction → edema

congenital-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established pediatric cardiology teaching.

cystic-fibrosis.name: Cystic fibrosis
cystic-fibrosis.scope: CFTR mutations, meconium ileus, bronchiectasis, pancreatic insufficiency, sweat chloride test
cystic-fibrosis.core: Recurrent sinopulmonary infection plus malabsorption, poor growth or neonatal meconium ileus suggests CFTR dysfunction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive CFTR variants; affected sibling or carrier parents
F508del is common; genotype determines eligibility for specific CFTR modulators

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic productive cough, recurrent pneumonia, nasal polyps, clubbing and bronchiectasis
Greasy stools, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency, failure to thrive despite appetite
Salty skin, dehydration with hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis; male infertility from absent vas deferens
Neonatal abdominal distention with inspissated ileal meconium; later rectal prolapse possible

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Defective apical chloride/bicarbonate transport → dehydrated airway and pancreatic secretions
Sweat ducts fail to reabsorb chloride; pancreatic duct blockage causes exocrine destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Positive newborn immunoreactive trypsinogen screen → **quantitative sweat chloride** confirmation
★ Sweat chloride **≥60 mmol/L** supports CF; 30–59 intermediate → repeat/genetic evaluation
Two CF-causing variants in trans or specialized CFTR-function testing resolve uncertain cases
Fecal elastase assesses pancreatic insufficiency; sputum cultures guide respiratory antibiotics
Consider CF despite negative limited mutation panel when clinical phenotype is compelling

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Daily **airway clearance**, hypertonic saline, dornase alfa; exercise supports mucus clearance
Pulmonary exacerbation → culture-directed antibiotics; Pseudomonas commonly needs antipseudomonal coverage
★ Pancreatic insufficiency → **pancrelipase with meals**, high-calorie nutrition, vitamins A/D/E/K
Eligible genotype → elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor; check liver function and interactions
Advanced respiratory failure → oxygen/ventilatory support and lung transplant assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Pseudomonas colonization, massive hemoptysis, pneumothorax, respiratory failure
CF-related diabetes, biliary liver disease, distal intestinal obstruction, osteoporosis and infertility

rows.label: Prevention
items: Vaccination, nutrition monitoring, salt/fluid replacement during heat or exercise
Infection-control separation between CF patients; family carrier testing and reproductive counseling

rows.label: Mimics
items: Primary ciliary dyskinesia: situs inversus possible; normal pancreatic function/sweat chloride
Immunodeficiency: recurrent infection without CFTR-pattern salt loss
Celiac disease: malabsorption without bronchiectasis

cystic-fibrosis.evidence: Diagnostic threshold checked 2026-10-30: [CF Foundation sweat testing](https://www.cff.org/intro-cf/sweat-test); management established CF teaching.

dementia.name: Dementia
dementia.scope: Alzheimer, vascular, Lewy body, frontotemporal, reversible causes, normal cognitive aging vs MCI, Parkinson disease dementia
dementia.core: Acquired cognitive decline interfering with independent daily function; distinguish dementia from normal aging and mild cognitive impairment by functional consequences.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced age: strongest Alzheimer risk; early-onset first-degree family history; Down syndrome (APP triplication)
Vascular risk factors, prior stroke, Parkinson disease
Anticholinergics, sedatives, alcohol, hearing loss, sleep apnea may worsen cognition

rows.label: Clues
items: Collateral history: missed bills/medications, getting lost, unsafe cooking or driving
Personality, language, executive, visuospatial, memory, motor symptoms help establish phenotype
Abrupt change, fluctuating attention, fever, focal deficits → evaluate acute superimposed illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alzheimer: amyloid plaques/tau tangles; Lewy/Parkinson: alpha-synuclein; vascular disease: ischemic neuronal injury
Alzheimer: hippocampal loss → poor delayed/episodic recall; **nucleus basalis of Meynert** loss → acetylcholine deficit
Frontotemporal degeneration affects frontal/anterior temporal networks, often before typical late-life onset

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Patient/informant history, cognition, function**; MoCA/MMSE support diagnosis, cannot establish it alone
★ **CBC, CMP, TSH, B12**, depression/medication review; HIV/syphilis testing if risk
Brain MRI or noncontrast CT → infarcts, mass, subdural, hydrocephalus; avoid routine PET as first test
Normal aging: slower retrieval, preserved independence → reassurance; MCI: objective deficit, independence preserved
Typical Alzheimer: clinical diagnosis after routine labs/imaging; **APOE genotyping not indicated**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Alzheimer/Lewy/Parkinson dementia → **donepezil or rivastigmine**; moderate/severe Alzheimer → add memantine
Vascular disease → BP/lipid/diabetes control, stroke prevention; frontotemporal behavioral symptoms → consider SSRI
★ Agitation → seek pain/infection, routines/redirection first; **avoid typical antipsychotics in Lewy/Parkinson disease**
Early biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer: specialist-selected antiamyloid drugs; baseline/serial MRI for ARIA
Parkinson dementia psychosis/agitation → **quetiapine** over haloperidol; clozapine needs agranulocytosis monitoring

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, aspiration, malnutrition, wandering, caregiver burnout; antipsychotics → increased mortality
Cholinesterase inhibitors → bradycardia, syncope, GI effects; antiamyloid antibodies → edema/microhemorrhage
Parkinson disease: dementia strongest predictor of nursing home placement and mortality

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Driving/home safety, advance planning**, caregiver support; assess decision-specific capacity
Visuospatial deficit, e.g., failed pentagon copy → **no car keys** until formal driving assessment
Exercise, hearing correction, social engagement, vascular risk reduction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Delirium: hours–days, impaired attention, fluctuating awareness
Depression: prominent distress, variable effort, potentially reversible cognitive deficits
Normal-pressure hydrocephalus: gait-first decline, incontinence, ventriculomegaly; tap test may predict shunt response

table.title: Phenotype clues
rows: Insidious episodic-memory decline, later multidomain deficits
Stroke-related or stepwise decline, focal findings
Early hallucinations, fluctuation, REM behavior, parkinsonism
Early disinhibition/apathy or progressive aphasia; memory spared
Established motor disease >1 year before dementia

dementia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [Alzheimer's Association diagnostic guidance 2024](https://www.alz.org/news/2024/clinical-practice-guideline-evaluation-alzheimers), [NICE dementia](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng97/chapter/Recommendations/); established subtype teaching.

depressive-disorders.name: Depressive disorders
depressive-disorders.scope: Major depressive disorder criteria, depression in older adults, bereavement vs MDD, pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, suicide risk
depressive-disorders.core: Persistent low mood or loss of pleasure with neurovegetative and cognitive symptoms, causing clinically significant distress or impaired function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior episodes, family history, chronic illness/pain, substance use, postpartum period, social isolation
Older adults: disability, bereavement, polypharmacy; somatic presentations

rows.label: Clues
items: SIGECAPS: sleep, interest, guilt, energy, concentration, appetite, psychomotor change, suicidality
Psychotic depression: delusions/hallucinations only during mood episodes, often guilt or nihilism
★ **Suicide risk**: prior attempt, intent, plan, means, agitation, psychosis, intoxication
Youth: **irritable mood** qualifies; academic decline, withdrawal, somatic complaints; not normal teenage behavior

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Multifactorial mood-circuit dysfunction involving monoamines, **HPA hyperactivity with raised cortisol**, and neuroplasticity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ MDD: **≥5 symptoms for ≥2 weeks**, including depressed mood or anhedonia; exclude mania/hypomania
Screen all adults, even asymptomatic: PHQ-2, PHQ-9 for severity; older adults: **Geriatric Depression Scale**
Interview establishes diagnosis; assess substances, drugs, TSH/CBC when clinically suspected
★ **Ask directly about suicide**, access to firearms, protective factors; questioning does not increase risk
Post-CABG anhedonia, withdrawal, fatigue → depression screen; vein-harvest leg edema expected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Imminent danger or **severe malnutrition** → **observation, psychiatric hospitalization**; remove lethal means
Mild: CBT/interpersonal therapy; moderate/severe: sertraline + psychotherapy; pregnancy → shared risk–benefit discussion
★ Urgent suicidality/catatonia/anorexia → **ECT**; psychotic depression → ECT or antidepressant + antipsychotic
Alternatives: **bupropion** (fatigue/hypersomnia, smoking cessation), **mirtazapine** (poor appetite, insomnia)
Continue antidepressant ≥6 months after remission; recurrent/severe episodes → longer maintenance

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, malnutrition, functional decline, recurrence
SSRIs: sexual dysfunction, GI effects, hyponatremia; early activation/suicidality monitoring, especially age <25
Bupropion: seizures; avoid with eating disorders, seizure disorders or brain tumor; mirtazapine: weight gain/sedation
Benzodiazepines in older adults: worsen depression, sedation, falls → stop, use antidepressant

rows.label: Prevention
items: Safety plan, early follow-up after drug changes
Taper antidepressants to reduce discontinuation symptoms; avoid antidepressant monotherapy in bipolar disorder

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dementia: insidious consistent deficits; **pseudodementia**: subacute, "I don't know" answers, recall improves with prompting
Hypothyroidism: cold intolerance, constipation, elevated TSH
Untreated OSA: snoring, obesity, sleepiness → **mood disorder due to medical condition**, not MDD
Anorexia nervosa: fear of weight gain, distorted body image

table.title: Distinguishing persistent sadness
rows: Waves tied to reminders; self-esteem usually preserved
Pervasive worthlessness; bereavement does not exclude diagnosis
Stressor within 3 months; MDD criteria absent

diverticular-disease.name: Diverticular disease
diverticular-disease.scope: Diverticulosis, acute diverticulitis, complicated diverticulitis (abscess, perforation, fistula), CT imaging, antibiotic therapy
diverticular-disease.core: Diverticulosis can bleed without pain; inflamed diverticula cause focal abdominal pain, with CT distinguishing uncomplicated disease from abscess or perforation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, obesity, smoking, low physical activity; regular NSAID use
Immunosuppression increases severity and can blunt fever or peritoneal findings

rows.label: Clues
items: Left lower quadrant tenderness, fever, leukocytosis, altered bowel habits
★ **Pneumaturia, fecaluria, recurrent polymicrobial UTI** → colovesical fistula
Peritoneal signs, hypotension, persistent vomiting → complicated disease requiring hospital evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosa/submucosa herniate through muscular weak points at penetrating vessels
Diverticular inflammation causes localized microperforation; adjacent vessel erosion causes arterial bleeding

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspected first/severe episode → **CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast**
Colonic wall thickening and pericolic stranding support inflammation; assess abscess, free air, obstruction
★ **Avoid colonoscopy during acute inflammation**; perforation risk
Colonoscopy after recovery for complicated disease, alarm findings, or overdue cancer screening; usually wait 6–8 weeks

rows.label: Tx
items: Low-risk uncomplicated disease: oral hydration, analgesia, advance diet as symptoms improve; antibiotics selective
★ Frail, immunocompromised, systemically ill, or complicated → **antibiotics** covering gram-negatives/anaerobes
Outpatient: amoxicillin-clavulanate (older exams: ciprofloxacin/metronidazole); severe: ceftriaxone/metronidazole or pip-tazo
Small abscess: antibiotics; larger accessible abscess, often >3 cm → percutaneous drainage
★ Peritonitis, uncontrolled sepsis, obstruction → **urgent surgery**; fistula → elective resection after stabilization

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, free perforation, stricture, fistula; recurrence does not automatically require colectomy
Severe diverticular hemorrhage may require colonoscopic hemostasis or angiographic embolization

rows.label: Prevention
items: Fiber-rich diet after recovery, exercise, weight management, smoking cessation
No need to avoid nuts, seeds, popcorn; avoid regular NSAIDs when possible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Colon cancer: progressive symptoms, weight loss, iron deficiency; can coexist
Ischemic colitis: sudden cramping then hematochezia, vascular risk
IBS: recurrent pain without fever or objective inflammation

eating-disorders.name: Eating disorders
eating-disorders.scope: Anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, binge eating disorder, refeeding syndrome, medical complications, hospitalization criteria
eating-disorders.core: Disordered intake or compensatory behaviors require assessment of medical instability, suicidality, and malnutrition at any body size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Adolescence, dieting, weight stigma, perfectionism, trauma; psychiatric comorbidity and family history

rows.label: Clues
items: Restrictive disease: cold intolerance, lanugo, bradycardia, orthostasis, menstrual suppression; amenorrhea not required
Purging: parotid hypertrophy, **raised amylase**, enamel erosion, knuckle calluses; hypokalemic hypochloremic alkalosis
★ **Syncope, arrhythmia, hypothermia or severe electrolyte abnormalities** → urgent stabilization

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Starvation suppresses gonadal axis and reduces cardiac mass; vomiting causes chloride/volume depletion
Refeeding insulin surge shifts phosphate, potassium and magnesium intracellularly

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical interview plus weight trajectory, vitals/orthostatics, **ECG, electrolytes, Mg, phosphate**
Binge: loss of control plus unusually large intake; bulimia/BED require episodes ≥weekly for 3 months
Assess suicide risk, substance use, exercise, laxatives; normal BMI does not exclude severe disease

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Medical admission for instability: e.g., HR <50, BP <90/60, severe electrolyte disturbance or acute food refusal
★ Refeeding → **thiamine**, nutritional rehabilitation, serial phosphate/K/Mg and cardiac monitoring
Adolescent anorexia → family-based treatment; adults → eating-disorder-focused psychotherapy; medication alone insufficient
Bulimia → CBT plus fluoxetine; avoid bupropion because of seizures
BED → CBT; lisdexamfetamine for selected adults, monitor misuse/cardiovascular risk

rows.label: Complications
items: Hypoestrogenism → osteoporosis, infertility; cardiac failure, arrhythmic death; purging → arrhythmias, esophageal injury
Refeeding → hypophosphatemia, respiratory failure, edema, delirium; high suicide mortality
Severe starvation → **hypoalbuminemia** with pitting edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Early recognition of growth/weight-trajectory changes; reduce weight-based stigma; relapse follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperthyroidism: increased appetite with tremor and heat intolerance
GI malabsorption: involuntary weight loss without weight/shape-driven restriction

eating-disorders.evidence: Guideline framework checked 2026-10-30: [APA eating disorders guideline, 2023](https://www.psychiatry.org/psychiatrists/practice/clinical-practice-guidelines/eating-disorders); thresholds: established clinical teaching.

table.title: Diagnostic distinction
rows: Restriction or purging + weight-gain fear/distorted self-image

encephalitis.name: Encephalitis
encephalitis.scope: Herpes simplex virus (HSV-1), temporal lobe lesions, CSF analysis (elevated RBCs, lymphocytic pleocytosis, PCR), IV acyclovir, West Nile virus, autoimmune encephalitis
encephalitis.core: Fever with sustained altered mental status, seizures, or focal neurologic deficits suggests brain inflammation and warrants immediate empiric acyclovir.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HSV-1 often occurs without immunosuppression; mosquito exposure suggests arboviruses
Autoimmune disease or tumor association; anti-NMDA receptor disease sometimes accompanies ovarian teratoma
Neonate, days–weeks old: perinatal HSV → seizures, fever, CSF RBCs, negative Gram stain

rows.label: Clues
items: HSV: personality change, aphasia, olfactory hallucinations, focal seizures
★ **Temporal lobe abnormalities** strongly suggest HSV; hemorrhagic CSF possible but not required
West Nile: movement disorder or asymmetric flaccid weakness; anti-NMDA: psychosis, dyskinesia, autonomic instability
Paraneoplastic limbic: **small cell lung cancer**, subacute psychosis/memory loss, medial temporal lesions, negative HSV PCR

rows.label: Pathophys
items: HSV causes necrotizing inflammation, often limbic/temporal; mosquito-borne viruses infect neuronal tissue
Autoantibodies against neuronal surface antigens disrupt synaptic signaling

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **LP: CSF cells, protein, glucose, HSV PCR**; lymphocytes, ↑protein, usually normal glucose
Neuroimaging before LP for focal deficits, papilledema, marked impaired consciousness, or suspected mass effect
MRI more sensitive than CT; EEG identifies nonconvulsive seizures or temporal periodic discharges
Early negative PCR with strong suspicion → continue treatment and repeat CSF PCR in 3–7 days
West Nile: CSF IgM; autoimmune suspicion → CSF/serum antibodies and tumor search

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected HSV → **IV acyclovir immediately**, usually 14–21 days; do not await PCR
Airway/seizure support; possible bacterial infection → ceftriaxone + vancomycin; Listeria risk → add ampicillin
Acyclovir: renal adjustment, IV hydration; West Nile: supportive care
★ Autoimmune disease → **steroids, IVIG/plasma exchange**, tumor removal after infectious evaluation
Reduced consciousness, status epilepticus, or respiratory compromise → ICU-level care

rows.label: Complications
items: Persistent memory impairment, epilepsy, focal deficits, death; acyclovir crystal nephropathy
Severe autoimmune disease: arrhythmia, hypoventilation, prolonged rehabilitation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mosquito repellent, protective clothing, vector control; no routine HSV encephalitis vaccine

rows.label: Mimics
items: Bacterial meningitis: neutrophilic CSF, low glucose; overlap requires empiric coverage
Toxic/metabolic delirium: systemic explanation without inflammatory CSF
Primary psychosis: lacks new seizures, dysautonomia, or focal neurologic abnormalities
Rabies: animal/bat exposure, **hydrophobia**, hypersalivation, agitation

encephalitis.evidence: Not checked online; established infectious and autoimmune neurology teaching.

endometriosis.name: Endometriosis
endometriosis.scope: Pelvic endometriosis, deep infiltrating endometriosis, endometrioma (chocolate cyst), uterosacral nodularity, cyclic pelvic pain, dyspareunia, laparoscopy, medical management
endometriosis.core: Reproductive-age patient with progressive cyclic pelvic pain, deep dyspareunia, and infertility from ectopic endometrial tissue.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Early menarche, short cycles, prolonged menstruation, family history; obstructed menstrual outflow

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Uterosacral nodularity**, fixed retroverted uterus, posterior cul-de-sac tenderness
Dyschezia or cyclic rectal bleeding → bowel involvement; urinary cyclic symptoms → bladder disease
Pain severity poorly correlates with lesion burden; examination may be normal

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Estrogen-responsive implants provoke inflammation, fibrosis, adhesions, and distortion of pelvic anatomy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical assessment + **transvaginal ultrasound** first; normal imaging cannot exclude superficial disease
MRI maps deep lesions or indeterminate adnexal masses; CA-125 not a diagnostic test
★ **Laparoscopy with biopsy**: definitive test; for uncertain diagnosis, refractory symptoms, or planned operative treatment
Current ACOG: presumptive clinical diagnosis, no surgery before empiric treatment; older exams may expect laparoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pain, no immediate pregnancy goal → **NSAID + continuous combined OCP** or progestin
Persistent symptoms → GnRH agonist/antagonist with add-back hormones to limit hypoestrogenic adverse effects
Refractory disease or selected infertility → laparoscopic excision/ablation and adhesiolysis
Endometrioma surgery may reduce ovarian reserve; balance pain, suspicion, size, and fertility goals
Trying to conceive → fertility evaluation; hormonal suppression does not improve spontaneous conception

rows.label: Complications
items: Adhesive infertility, bowel/ureteral obstruction, chronic pain; small increase in clear-cell/endometrioid ovarian cancer
GnRH suppression → hot flashes, bone loss; disease may recur after conservative surgery

rows.label: Prevention
items: Postoperative hormonal suppression reduces pain recurrence when pregnancy not desired; no established primary prevention

rows.label: Mimics
items: Adenomyosis: diffusely enlarged, boggy uterus with heavy bleeding
PID: fever, discharge, cervical motion tenderness; pain less cyclic
Primary dysmenorrhea: normal examination, onset soon after menarche, no structural lesion

table.title: Anatomic forms
rows: Fibrotic nodules involving ligaments, bowel, bladder
Ovarian chocolate cyst; homogeneous ground-glass ultrasound echoes

essential-hypertension.name: Essential hypertension
essential-hypertension.scope: Blood pressure staging, nonpharmacologic interventions (weight loss, DASH, exercise), first-line antihypertensive agents, resistant hypertension
essential-hypertension.core: Persistently elevated arterial pressure usually reflects multifactorial primary hypertension; confirm accurate repeated measurements before long-term treatment decisions.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, family history, obesity, excess sodium/alcohol, inactivity, poor sleep
NSAIDs, stimulants, oral contraceptives can raise BP; assess before labeling primary disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; headache alone does not establish hypertensive emergency
★ **Acute target-organ injury** with severe pressure → hypertensive emergency; BP number alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased vascular resistance, altered renal sodium handling, sympathetic/RAAS activation sustain elevated pressure
Chronic endothelial injury accelerates atherosclerosis and small-vessel organ damage
Older adults: large-artery stiffness (low compliance) → **isolated systolic hypertension**, wide pulse pressure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Average ≥2 readings on ≥2 visits; confirm using **home BP or ambulatory monitoring**
Rest seated, feet supported, correct cuff, arm at heart level; avoid recent caffeine/exercise
BMP, creatinine/eGFR, urinalysis/albuminuria, lipids, glucose/A1c, ECG assess risk and injury
Resistant: above goal on 3 agents including diuretic, or controlled on ≥4; exclude pseudoresistance
Child/adolescent high oscillometric reading → **confirm by auscultation** before ambulatory monitoring or workup

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **DASH diet, weight reduction, sodium restriction, aerobic activity**, moderate alcohol; target generally <130/80
≥140/90 → drugs, usually two classes; ≥130/80 with CVD, diabetes, CKD, or PREVENT ≥7.5% → drugs
★ Low-risk stage 1: **3–6 months lifestyle**, then drugs if still ≥130/80; updated 2025 threshold
Initial: chlorthalidone, amlodipine, lisinopril, or losartan; albuminuric CKD → ACE inhibitor/ARB (older exams: any diabetes)
Resistant after optimized triple regimen → spironolactone; monitor K/creatinine; never combine ACE inhibitor + ARB

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, MI, LV hypertrophy/HF, CKD, retinopathy, aortic disease
Thiazide: low Na/K, gout; ACE inhibitor: cough/angioedema; RAAS drugs contraindicated in pregnancy

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication adherence, home readings, regular follow-up; assess orthostatic symptoms in older adults
Weight loss: largest lifestyle BP drop, ~1 mm Hg/kg; smoking cessation barely lowers resting BP
BP control: largest modifiable stroke-risk reduction; also prevents concentric LVH and HF

rows.label: Mimics
items: White-coat hypertension: office high, home normal
Masked hypertension: elevated out-of-office only; secondary causes: abrupt/refractory pressure with renal/endocrine clues

extremity-vascular-injury.name: Extremity vascular injury
extremity-vascular-injury.scope: Hard signs (pulsatile bleeding, expanding hematoma, absent pulses, thrill/bruit, pallor), soft signs (diminished pulse, proximity), surgical exploration vs CT angiography
extremity-vascular-injury.core: After limb trauma, active arterial bleeding or threatened perfusion requires immediate intervention; stable equivocal findings require objective vascular assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Penetrating wounds near major vessels; blunt crush or traction injury
Knee dislocation, supracondylar humeral fracture, open fractures; spontaneous joint reduction may conceal mechanism

rows.label: Clues
items: Pain, pallor, coolness, paresthesia, paralysis indicate worsening ischemia; motor deficit is late
★ **Normal distal pulses do not exclude injury**, especially intimal tears after knee dislocation
Examine both limbs and document pulses, motor function, sensation before and after reduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transection causes hemorrhage; intimal disruption → thrombosis and delayed ischemia
Contained arterial leak → pseudoaneurysm; artery–vein communication → traumatic AV fistula

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Hard signs → immediate **operative exploration**; imaging must not delay limb-saving treatment
Stable without hard signs → ABI/API; **<0.9** or abnormal examination → CT angiography
Normal examination + index ≥0.9 → serial examinations/follow-up; observe high-risk blunt injuries
Duplex ultrasound alternative in selected stable patients; CTA localizes injury for repair

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Direct pressure; uncontrolled hemorrhage → proximal tourniquet; avoid blind clamping
Resuscitate hemorrhagic shock with blood products; urgent vascular surgery consultation
★ Restore arterial flow rapidly, ideally within 6 hours; primary repair or vein graft
Temporary shunt when definitive repair delayed; coordinate fracture stabilization and revascularization
Prolonged ischemia, crush injury, marked swelling → early fasciotomy; monitor reperfusion hyperkalemia

rows.label: Complications
items: Amputation, persistent neuropathy, compartment syndrome; rhabdomyolysis and AKI after reperfusion
Delayed thrombosis, pseudoaneurysm, AV fistula, graft infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: Repeat neurovascular checks after splinting, reduction, and repair; promptly loosen constrictive dressings
Discharge follow-up essential for delayed swelling, recurrent bleeding, bruit, or new ischemic symptoms

rows.label: Mimics
items: Compartment syndrome: pain with passive stretch, tense compartments; pulses often remain palpable
Isolated nerve injury: focal deficits without objective perfusion abnormality

table.title: Trauma signs
rows: Absent pulses; bruit/thrill; overt distal ischemia
Diminished pulse; stable hematoma; prior bleeding

gallstone-disease.name: Gallstone disease
gallstone-disease.scope: Biliary colic, acute cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis, cholangitis, gallstone pancreatitis
gallstone-disease.core: Gallstone location determines the syndrome: transient cystic obstruction, gallbladder inflammation, common-duct obstruction/infection, or pancreatic inflammation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Age, female sex, pregnancy, obesity, rapid weight loss, ileal disease/resection
Hemolysis/cirrhosis → pigment stones; critical illness/TPN → acalculous cholecystitis

rows.label: Clues
items: Postprandial RUQ/epigastric discomfort radiating to back or right shoulder; assess fever and jaundice
★ **Fever + RUQ pain + jaundice** → cholangitis; hypotension/confusion → severe infection
Pancreatitis: persistent epigastric pain radiating to back, vomiting; ALT >150 supports biliary cause

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Cholesterol supersaturation or pigment precipitation creates calculi; obstruction location dictates organ injury
Infected obstructed bile ducts require drainage because antibiotics cannot reliably sterilize a closed system

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **RUQ ultrasound first**; CBC, bilirubin/alkaline phosphatase, AST/ALT, lipase
Suspected cholecystitis with equivocal ultrasound → HIDA; nonvisualized gallbladder supports cystic-duct obstruction
Intermediate common-duct stone probability → MRCP or EUS; ERCP reserved primarily for treatment
★ Direct intervention: **stone seen, cholangitis, or bilirubin >4 mg/dL plus dilated duct**
Post-cholecystectomy jaundice + dilated ducts → retained stone/duct injury → **ERCP**; HIDA only for bile leak

rows.label: Tx
items: Analgesia, fluids, antiemetics; infection → ceftriaxone/metronidazole or piperacillin/tazobactam
★ **Cholangitis → urgent biliary drainage**, immediately after stabilization if shock; do not await antibiotic response
Poor surgical candidate with acute cholecystitis → percutaneous cholecystostomy
★ Gallstone pancreatitis → supportive care, early oral feeding; **no urgent ERCP without cholangitis/persistent obstruction**

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, gangrene, perforation, abscess, septic shock; pancreatitis → necrosis/organ failure
Cholecystoenteric fistula → gallstone ileus; imaging: bowel obstruction, pneumobilia, ectopic stone
ERCP → pancreatitis/bleeding/perforation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain healthy weight; avoid rapid weight loss; selected bariatric patients → ursodiol prophylaxis
After duct clearance → cholecystectomy; after mild biliary pancreatitis → same-admission cholecystectomy
Asymptomatic uncomplicated stones → observation; no routine prophylactic surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hepatitis: marked aminotransferase elevation, no obstructing stone
PUD: burning epigastric pain, ulcer on endoscopy
Inferior MI: ischemic ECG/troponin changes, cardiovascular risk

table.title: Localizing obstruction
rows: Persistent >6 hours, Murphy sign, wall thickening
Cholestatic labs, duct stone/dilation; no infection
ERCP extraction or operative duct clearance
Inflamed gallbladder without stones; critically ill

glomerulonephritis.name: Glomerulonephritis
glomerulonephritis.scope: Nephritic syndrome, poststreptococcal GN, IgA nephropathy, rapidly progressive GN (anti-GBM, ANCA), lupus nephritis, RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs, proteinuria quantification, kidney biopsy
glomerulonephritis.core: Glomerular inflammation causes hematuria, proteinuria, hypertension, edema, and reduced filtration; rapidly rising creatinine demands urgent evaluation for crescentic disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent streptococcal pharyngitis/skin infection, systemic autoimmunity, small-vessel vasculitis
IgA nephropathy often follows mucosal infection; anti-GBM pulmonary bleeding risk increases with smoking

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **RBC casts and dysmorphic RBCs** identify a glomerular bleeding source
Tea-colored urine, oliguria, periorbital swelling; nephrotic-range protein loss can coexist
★ **Hemoptysis + AKI** → pulmonary–renal syndrome; rapidly progressive disease may initially lack systemic symptoms

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune complexes, basement-membrane antibodies, or pauci-immune vascular injury inflame glomerular capillaries
Crescent formation compresses capillary tufts → rapid, potentially irreversible loss of filtration
Reduced filtration → sodium/water retention → **volume overload**, edema, hypertension

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Urinalysis/microscopy → **creatinine, electrolytes, urine protein/creatinine ratio**; monitor urine output
C3/C4, ANA/dsDNA, ANCA, anti-GBM; ASO/anti-DNase B when poststreptococcal disease suspected
★ **Kidney biopsy** for rapidly progressive AKI, substantial persistent proteinuria, or uncertain systemic GN
Typical childhood poststreptococcal course may not require biopsy; persistent low C3 beyond 8 weeks warrants reassessment

rows.label: Tx
items: Salt restriction, loop diuretics for overload, BP control; ACE inhibitor/ARB for persistent proteinuria when stable
★ Pulmonary–renal/RPGN → **urgent nephrology, steroids + immunosuppression** before irreversible decline
Anti-GBM: plasma exchange + cyclophosphamide; ANCA: rituximab/cyclophosphamide; plasma exchange only selected severe cases
Lupus: biopsy-directed mycophenolate/cyclophosphamide + steroids; poststreptococcal disease mainly supportive

rows.label: Complications
items: Hyperkalemia, pulmonary edema, hypertensive emergency, CKD; dialysis for refractory life-threatening derangements
Immunosuppression → infection, cytopenias, infertility with cyclophosphamide

rows.label: Prevention
items: Control BP/proteinuria, avoid nephrotoxins, follow renal function and urine findings

rows.label: Mimics
items: ATN: muddy-brown casts after ischemia/toxins
Urologic bleeding: isomorphic RBCs, clots, no RBC casts

glomerulonephritis.evidence: Not checked online; established nephrology teaching.

gout.name: Gout and crystal arthropathy
gout.scope: Acute gout, chronic gout and urate lowering, pseudogout (CPPD)
gout.core: Abrupt intensely painful inflammatory arthritis from crystal deposition; gout and CPPD require different long-term prevention despite similar flare management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Gout: CKD, obesity, alcohol, purines/fructose, thiazide/loop diuretics, low-dose aspirin
CPPD: older age, joint injury, hyperparathyroidism, hemochromatosis, hypomagnesemia
Flares follow surgery, dehydration, illness, or changes in urate concentration

rows.label: Clues
items: Rapid-onset red swollen tender joint, often overnight; fever possible
Chronic gout: tophi on ears/olecranon, erosive arthritis; recurrent flares separated by asymptomatic intervals
CPPD in younger adults → investigate associated metabolic disorders

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Crystal phagocytosis activates inflammasome/IL-1 → neutrophilic synovitis
Most hyperuricemia reflects reduced renal urate excretion rather than excessive production

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ First/atypical acute monoarthritis → **arthrocentesis**, polarized microscopy, Gram stain/culture
★ **Crystals do not exclude septic arthritis**; serum urate may be normal during gout flare
Chronic imaging: punched-out defects with overhanging edges; ultrasound double-contour sign supports urate deposition

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute crystal flare → **indomethacin/other NSAID, colchicine, or glucocorticoid**; joint steroid after excluding infection
NSAID failure → switch class; older exam questions may expect potent NSAID, e.g. indomethacin
CKD/ulcer/anticoagulation → favor steroid; adjust colchicine for renal impairment/interactions; avoid NSAIDs in advanced CKD
★ Urate lowering: **allopurinol first-line**, including CKD; start low, titrate to serum urate <6 mg/dL
Urate lowering doesn't treat flares; continue through flares; may start mid-flare (older exam questions: wait)

rows.label: Complications
items: Gout: destructive arthritis, uric-acid stones; CPPD: chronic degenerative/inflammatory arthropathy
Allopurinol hypersensitivity; colchicine → diarrhea/neuromyopathy
Xanthine-oxidase inhibitors + azathioprine/6-MP → severe marrow suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Urate lowering: **tophi, joint damage, ≥2 flares/year**; first flare with CKD ≥3/stones/urate >9 → consider
Starting urate lowering → colchicine/NSAID prophylaxis 3–6 months; serial urate monitoring; not for isolated hyperuricemia
Uncomplicated first flare → **limit alcohol/fructose**, lose weight; thiazide → losartan; keep indicated aspirin
Before allopurinol: HLA-B*58:01 testing with Southeast Asian/African American ancestry; CPPD lacks crystal-depleting drugs

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic arthritis: positive culture, bacteremia risk; aspiration essential when uncertain
Cellulitis: superficial inflammation, less restriction of passive joint motion
RA: persistent symmetric small-joint synovitis

gout.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACR gout guideline 2020](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10563586/), [ACR gout education 2025](https://rheumatology.org/patients/gout); CPPD established teaching.

heart-failure.name: Heart failure
heart-failure.scope: HFrEF, HFpEF, acute decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic flash pulmonary edema, guideline-directed medical therapy, neurohormonal activation (RAAS, ADH-mediated hyponatremia)
heart-failure.core: Inadequate cardiac output or elevated filling pressures → pulmonary or systemic congestion, even with a normal ejection fraction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CAD, hypertension, valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, alcohol, cardiotoxic chemotherapy
Decompensation triggers: ischemia, infection, arrhythmia, missed diuretics, NSAIDs

rows.label: Clues
items: Orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, elevated JVP, crackles or wheeze (cardiac asthma), dependent edema
S3 suggests volume overload; S4 suggests stiff ventricle
★ **Flash edema**: abrupt respiratory distress, severe hypertension, pink frothy sputum

rows.label: Pathophys
items: RAAS/sympathetic activation → vasoconstriction, sodium retention, adverse remodeling
Low effective volume → baroreceptor-driven nonosmotic **ADH** release → dilutional hyponatremia; marker of advanced disease
Alveolar flooding → V/Q mismatch, widened A-a gradient, hypoxemia
High-output HF: severe anemia, AV fistula (larger fistula → more shunt); HF signs with **normal/high EF**

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography**: EF, valves, wall motion; ECG, CXR, BNP support diagnosis
Low BNP argues against HF; obesity lowers BNP, renal dysfunction raises it
Identify precipitant: troponin, CBC, electrolytes, creatinine; evaluate ischemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute congestion → **IV furosemide**; hypoxemia → oxygen; respiratory distress → noninvasive ventilation
★ Hypertensive pulmonary edema → **IV nitroglycerin**; shock → norepinephrine ± dobutamine, urgent cause correction
Congested HFrEF → loop diuretic + **ACE inhibitor/ARNI first**; beta-blocker/MRA once compensated; ACE inhibitor → ARNI: 36-hour washout
MRA: eGFR >30, K <5; never ACE inhibitor + ARB; EF ≤35% despite GDMT → consider ICD
HFrEF foundation drugs lower mortality; loop diuretics, nitrates alone, digoxin relieve symptoms only

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiorenal syndrome, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden death, hepatic congestion
Diuresis → hypokalemia; RAAS blockade → hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction; monitor creatinine/K

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Daily weights, sodium moderation, adherence; **continue GDMT after EF recovery**
Treat hypertension, CAD, AF; smoking cessation, exercise, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination

rows.label: Mimics
items: COPD: obstructive spirometry, hyperinflation
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia
PE: pleuritic pain, thrombotic risk, RV strain
ARDS: diffuse infiltrates, no cephalization; massive crystalloid + **cephalization/perihilar fullness** → volume overload

table.title: Chronic phenotypes
rows: Sacubitril/valsartan (or ACEi/ARB), carvedilol/metoprolol succinate, spironolactone, dapagliflozin

heart-failure.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC HFrEF 2024](https://www.acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/03/06/19/22/2024-acc-expert-consensus-hfref); other points established teaching.

heat-related-illness.name: Heat-related illness
heat-related-illness.scope: Heat exhaustion, classic and exertional heat stroke, malignant hyperthermia and NMS contrast
heat-related-illness.core: Heat exposure with neurologic dysfunction signals heat stroke, requiring immediate cooling before laboratory confirmation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Classic: older adults (**impaired thirst**), heat waves, impaired sweating, anticholinergics, limited water access
Exertional: strenuous activity, poor acclimatization, heavy equipment, stimulant use

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Delirium, seizures, or coma** distinguish heat stroke from uncomplicated heat exhaustion
Tachycardia, hypotension, vomiting; sweating may persist despite severe heat injury
Core temperature often >40 °C; lower readings after cooling do not exclude heat stroke

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Heat production exceeds dissipation → endothelial injury, systemic inflammation, cellular dysfunction
Sweat losses → hypovolemia; excessive free water intake can produce hyponatremia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Rectal temperature**; oral, axillary, and tympanic measurements may underestimate severity
CBC, electrolytes, creatinine, CK, urinalysis, liver enzymes, coagulation studies; repeat for evolving injury

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Airway support, remove clothing, **rapid whole-body cooling**; do not delay for transport or tests
Exertional: cold-water immersion, else evaporative cooling; classic: evaporative; no alcohol sponging; stop active cooling near 39 °C
★ **IV isotonic crystalloid** for hypovolemia; benzodiazepines for seizures or shivering
Avoid antipyretics; environmental hyperthermia has no elevated hypothalamic temperature set point

rows.label: Complications
items: Rhabdomyolysis, AKI, DIC, hepatic failure, ARDS, persistent neurologic deficits
Delayed liver injury despite initial clinical improvement

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Gradual acclimatization**, scheduled rest, shade, hydration, cooling access
Avoid strenuous exercise during peak heat; monitor vulnerable adults during heat waves

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sepsis: infectious focus, fever unrelated to environmental load
Serotonin syndrome: serotonergic exposure, clonus, hyperreflexia

heat-related-illness.evidence: Not checked online; established emergency medicine teaching.

hemochromatosis.name: Hemochromatosis
hemochromatosis.scope: Hereditary hemochromatosis, HFE gene mutations, iron overload, bronze diabetes, arthropathy, therapeutic phlebotomy
hemochromatosis.core: Progressive iron loading can unite liver disease, diabetes, pigmentation, cardiac dysfunction, and characteristic hand arthropathy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autosomal recessive HFE disease, especially C282Y homozygosity; northern European ancestry
Clinical expression later in men; menstruation/pregnancy delay iron accumulation in many women

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, hepatomegaly, elevated transaminases; bronze skin, hypogonadism, erectile dysfunction
★ **Second/third MCP arthropathy**, hook osteophytes or chondrocalcinosis with systemic iron features
Cardiomyopathy or arrhythmia may precede obvious hepatic disease; family history supports diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inadequate hepcidin signaling → excessive intestinal iron absorption
Unregulated tissue deposition generates oxidative injury in liver, pancreas, heart and pituitary

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Transferrin saturation and ferritin** first; TS ≥45% prompts HFE testing
Ferritin alone nonspecific: inflammation, alcohol and metabolic liver disease also elevate it
MRI quantifies hepatic iron; elastography assesses fibrosis; biopsy if staging/etiology remains uncertain
Ferritin >1,000 ng/mL or abnormal liver enzymes → evaluate advanced fibrosis/cirrhosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Therapeutic phlebotomy** for confirmed iron overload; monitor hemoglobin and ferritin
Frequency individualized by symptoms, hemoglobin recovery and iron stores; avoid inducing anemia
Chelation for iron overload when phlebotomy unsuitable, especially transfusion-dependent anemia
Treat diabetes, heart failure and hypogonadism; arthropathy often persists despite iron removal

rows.label: Complications
items: Cirrhosis and HCC risk, including after iron depletion once advanced fibrosis established
Restrictive/dilated cardiomyopathy, conduction disease, endocrine failure; Vibrio vulnificus infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Screen first-degree relatives** with iron studies/genetic counseling; avoid iron supplements and high-dose vitamin C
Avoid raw shellfish and excess alcohol; cirrhosis → HCC surveillance; hepatitis A/B vaccination

rows.label: Mimics
items: Inflammatory hyperferritinemia: saturation often normal/low
Transfusional siderosis: repeated RBC transfusions, underlying anemia rather than excess absorption

herpes-zoster.name: Herpes zoster
herpes-zoster.scope: Varicella zoster reactivation, dermatomal rash, herpes zoster ophthalmicus, Ramsay Hunt syndrome, oral antivirals, postherpetic neuralgia, Shingrix vaccine
herpes-zoster.core: Latent varicella-zoster reactivation causes painful unilateral dermatomal vesicles; ophthalmic involvement or disseminated disease changes urgency and treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, HIV, malignancy, transplantation, immunosuppressive drugs
Previous chickenpox or live varicella vaccination establishes latency; no new exposure required

rows.label: Clues
items: Burning/allodynia can precede eruption by days; crops crust over approximately 7–10 days
★ **V1 distribution, nasal-tip lesions, eye pain** → urgent ophthalmology for zoster ophthalmicus
★ **Ear vesicles + ipsilateral facial paralysis** ± hearing/vestibular symptoms → Ramsay Hunt syndrome
Multiple noncontiguous dermatomes or >20 lesions outside primary/adjacent dermatomes suggests dissemination

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced VZV-specific cellular immunity permits virus to travel from sensory ganglion to skin
Neuronal inflammation/injury explains acute pain and persistent neuropathic symptoms

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical eruption → **clinical diagnosis**; atypical lesions → vesicle-base VZV PCR
Assess ocular, neurologic, and systemic findings; consider immunodeficiency evaluation for unusually severe/recurrent disease
CSF PCR for suspected CNS infection; do not delay treatment in high-risk presentations

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Valacyclovir, famciclovir, or acyclovir** ideally within 72 hours; still treat new lesions or complications
Dissemination, visceral/CNS disease, severe immunosuppression → **IV acyclovir**
Acute pain: acetaminophen/NSAID, add neuropathic agent when needed; avoid routine systemic steroids
Ramsay Hunt: antiviral plus glucocorticoid early; eye lubrication/protection for incomplete closure
Postherpetic neuralgia: **gabapentin**/pregabalin, lidocaine patch; TCA anticholinergic in elderly; no late antiviral

rows.label: Complications
items: Persistent pain >90 days, secondary bacterial infection, corneal injury, vision loss
Meningoencephalitis, vasculopathy, visceral spread in vulnerable patients

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Shingrix two doses** for adults ≥50 years or immunocompromised ≥19 years, including prior zoster
Cover lesions, **avoid susceptible contacts** until crusted; exposure causes chickenpox, not immediate shingles
Disseminated: airborne/contact until crusted; immunocompromised localized: same precautions until dissemination excluded

rows.label: Mimics
items: HSV: recurrent localized lesions, often oral/genital rather than a full dermatome
Contact dermatitis: prominent itch, exposure pattern, no neuropathic prodrome

hiv-infection.name: HIV infection
hiv-infection.scope: Acute HIV, testing, ART start, opportunistic infection prophylaxis, PrEP/PEP, opportunistic infections (CMV retinitis, toxoplasmosis, PJP)
hiv-infection.core: HIV progressively depletes CD4 cells; early diagnosis and suppressive ART prevent immune failure and sexual transmission.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual exposure, shared injection equipment, perinatal transmission; other STIs increase acquisition risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Acute infection 2–4 weeks post-exposure: fever, rash, sore throat, **mucosal ulcers**, diarrhea, generalized lymphadenopathy
Weight loss, thrush, recurrent candida/herpes, **extensive adult molluscum** → test HIV; dysphagia → candidal esophagitis
Child/teen: chronic fever/diarrhea, poor growth, generalized nodes, splenomegaly, **polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retroviral integration creates lifelong reservoirs; ongoing replication drives immune depletion and inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Fourth-generation Ag/Ab → HIV-1/2 differentiation assay**; discordance → HIV RNA
★ Recent exposure/acute syndrome despite negative screen → **HIV RNA**, before antibodies appear
Baseline viral load, CD4, genotype, renal/liver function, HBV/HCV/TB, pregnancy testing, **cervical cytology**
AIDS: CD4 <200 or AIDS-defining illness regardless of count
Prenatal: opt-out screening; refusal → counsel, re-offer later; never test without consent

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Start **integrase-based ART promptly**, usually bictegravir/TAF/emtricitabine; assess HBV coinfection and interactions
Do not delay routine ART for genotype; cryptococcal/TB meningitis require disease-specific deferred timing
PJP: TMP-SMX; add glucocorticoid if PaO₂ <70 or A–a gradient ≥35
Toxoplasmosis: **pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/leucovorin**, else TMP-SMX; CMV retinitis: valganciclovir, ophthalmology
Untreated/viremic mother's newborn → **triple ART** ASAP, ideally within 6 h, ≤6 weeks; suppressed mother → zidovudine alone

rows.label: Complications
items: Opportunistic infections, malignancies, wasting, neurocognitive disease, kidney disease
Immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome after ART; drug toxicity/interactions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ PJP prophylaxis: **TMP-SMX** with CD4 <200 before/starting ART; on ART, <100 or 100–200 with viremia
Toxoplasma IgG positive + CD4 <100 → prophylaxis; MAC <50 only without immediate effective ART
★ Exposure ≤72 hours → **28-day PEP: dolutegravir + TDF/emtricitabine**; do not delay for laboratory results
PrEP: TDF/emtricitabine, cabotegravir, or lenacapavir; exclude HIV first, continue serial testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: EBV mononucleosis: atypical lymphocytes, heterophile positivity; acute HIV can be heterophile-negative
Primary CNS lymphoma: often solitary lesion; biopsy after failed empiric anti-Toxoplasma treatment, earlier if serology/imaging/CSF PCR disagree
SCID/CVID: low immunoglobulins; SCID lymphopenia, no nodes; perinatal HIV: PJP, thrush, nodes, normal lymphocytes

table.title: Advanced-disease syndromes
rows: Dry cough, hypoxemia, ground-glass; sputum/BAL silver stain
Ring-enhancing mass lesions, edema/mass effect; positive IgG
Cognitive decline; non-enhancing subcortical demyelination, no mass effect

human-papillomavirus-infection.name: Human papillomavirus infection
human-papillomavirus-infection.scope: Low-risk HPV and condyloma, high-risk oncogenic HPV (16, 18), anogenital intraepithelial neoplasia and carcinomas, HPV vaccination
human-papillomavirus-infection.core: Most HPV infections clear spontaneously; persistent oncogenic infection causes precancer, while low-risk types cause anogenital warts.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual skin-to-skin contact, new/multiple partners, immunosuppression, HIV
Smoking promotes persistent infection and cervical neoplasia; penetration not required for transmission

rows.label: Clues
items: Condyloma acuminata: painless flesh-colored, verrucous or cauliflower-like genital/perianal growths
High-risk infection usually asymptomatic; postcoital bleeding or abnormal cervical lesion needs diagnostic assessment
★ **Ulceration, induration, fixation, pigmentation, bleeding**, or nonresponse → biopsy rather than empiric retreatment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ★ **HPV 6/11** mainly cause warts; **16/18** account for major oncogenic risk
High-risk E6/E7 interfere with p53/Rb → dysplasia and invasive carcinoma

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Typical external warts → **visual diagnosis**; HPV testing does not guide wart management
Biopsy atypical lesions or uncertain diagnosis, especially with immunosuppression
Cervical HPV/cytology screens for neoplasia; abnormal results → risk-based colposcopy and directed biopsy
No routine HPV screening of asymptomatic partners or blood testing for infection
**Koilocytes** on Pap: perinuclear halo, irregular hyperchromatic nucleus → HPV effect/LSIL, not invasive carcinoma

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Warts: **imiquimod, podofilox, cryotherapy**, trichloroacetic acid by site/burden; older questions: podophyllum resin
Pregnancy: avoid podofilox/podophyllin; use clinician-applied cryotherapy or acid when treatment needed
High-grade intraepithelial lesions → site-specific ablation/excision; visible suspicious cancer → biopsy and staging
Treatment removes lesions without reliably eradicating virus; warts or asymptomatic infection: no antiviral

rows.label: Complications
items: Squamous carcinomas: cervical, anal (HIV), vulvar, vaginal, penile, oropharyngeal; recurrent respiratory papillomatosis
Warts frequently recur; treatment may cause local irritation, ulceration, pigment change

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **9-valent vaccine before exposure**; catch-up through 26 years, shared decision at 27–45 years
AAP: two doses starting <15 years; three if older/immunocompromised; federal 2026 policy differs
Vaccinated people still need cervical screening; condoms reduce but do not eliminate transmission

rows.label: Mimics
items: Condyloma lata: broad moist flat secondary-syphilis lesions, positive serology
Molluscum: smooth umbilicated papules; skin tags: soft pedunculated growths

hyperbilirubinemia.name: Hyperbilirubinemia
hyperbilirubinemia.scope: Gilbert syndrome, Crigler-Najjar, Dubin-Johnson, Rotor, unconjugated vs conjugated, biliary atresia
hyperbilirubinemia.core: Fractionate bilirubin first: indirect elevation reflects production or conjugation problems; direct elevation requires assessment of hepatobiliary excretion.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Fasting, illness or dehydration triggers Gilbert jaundice; family history suggests inherited bilirubin disorders
Persistent infant jaundice can reflect biliary atresia even after initially reassuring appearance

rows.label: Clues
items: Indirect bilirubin is albumin-bound and absent from urine; direct bilirubin can darken urine
★ Infant **pale/acholic stools**, dark urine, hepatomegaly → obstructive cholestasis
Pruritus, pale stools and elevated alkaline phosphatase suggest impaired bile flow
Severe neonatal indirect elevation with lethargy, poor feeding or abnormal tone → bilirubin neurotoxicity

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Heme breakdown yields unconjugated pigment; hepatic UGT conjugation enables biliary elimination
Unbound unconjugated bilirubin crosses the immature blood–brain barrier; conjugated bilirubin does not cause kernicterus
Large hematoma/cephalhematoma resorption → bilirubin overproduction, indirect jaundice

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Total/direct bilirubin**, AST/ALT, alkaline phosphatase/GGT; CBC/reticulocytes/LDH for suspected hemolysis
Isolated mild indirect elevation with normal liver tests and no hemolysis → Gilbert diagnosis
★ Jaundice beyond 2 weeks → fractionate; **direct ≥1 mg/dL at 2–4 weeks** → urgent referral
Infant cholestasis → ultrasound; biliary atresia assessment may require biopsy and operative cholangiography
Adult conjugated elevation with pain/obstruction → RUQ ultrasound before advanced duct imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected biliary atresia → urgent pediatric hepatology/surgery; **early Kasai portoenterostomy**
Severe neonatal indirect, even Coombs-positive → **phototherapy** first; exchange: failure, critical level, encephalopathy
Crigler–Najjar I → intensive phototherapy, definitive liver transplant; type II responds to phenobarbital
Gilbert, Dubin–Johnson and Rotor → reassurance once competing pathology excluded
Cholestasis → nutritional support, fat-soluble vitamins and cause-specific treatment

rows.label: Complications
items: Indirect neonatal hyperbilirubinemia → acute encephalopathy/kernicterus
Untreated atresia → cirrhosis, portal hypertension, liver failure

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Inspect stool color and fractionate persistent infant jaundice; never label conjugated jaundice physiologic

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hemolysis: anemia, reticulocytosis, low haptoglobin; newborn ABO: mother O, baby A/B, Coombs-positive
Choledochal cyst: cystic/dilated extrahepatic ducts on ultrasound
Physiologic jaundice: indirect, after 24 h, peaks days 3–5, thriving; transient UGT immaturity
Breast-milk jaundice: indirect, thriving; direct elevation excludes it

hyperbilirubinemia.evidence: Infant referral checked 2026-10-30: [AAP 2025](https://publications.aap.org/aapnews/news/pdfDownload/31302); inherited syndromes established teaching.

hyperglycemic-crises.name: Hyperglycemic crises
hyperglycemic-crises.core: Insulin-deficient diabetes with osmotic diuresis: rapid acidotic illness or slowly progressive hyperosmolar encephalopathy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Infection, missed insulin, pump failure, MI; DKA often type 1, HHS often older type 2
Euglycemic triggers: **SGLT2 inhibitors**, pregnancy, fasting

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, thirst, weight loss, dry mucosa, tachycardia
DKA: abdominal pain, vomiting, **Kussmaul (deep) breathing**; HHS: profound dehydration, focal deficits
★ Severe: **hypotension, stupor**, or coma → ICU

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insulin deficit + counterregulatory hormones → lipolysis, ketogenesis; residual insulin in HHS limits ketosis
Total-body K depleted despite initially normal/high serum K

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Glucose, electrolytes, venous pH, β-hydroxybutyrate**, osmolality; ECG + trigger evaluation
Effective osmolality = 2 × Na + glucose/18; glucose in mg/dL
★ HHS: **effective osmolality >300 OR total >320 mOsm/kg**; substantial ketosis/acidosis → mixed DKA/HHS
DKA resolution: ketones <0.6 mmol/L AND (pH ≥7.3 OR HCO₃ ≥18); urine ketones/anion gap misleading

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV isotonic crystalloid → K correction → IV regular insulin**; K <3.5 mmol/L → delay insulin
Replace K when <5 mmol/L; glucose checks every 1–2 h, electrolytes/pH/ketones every 4 h
★ Add **dextrose** below glucose 250; euglycemic presentation → immediately; continue insulin until crisis resolves
SC basal insulin overlaps infusion 1–2 h; bicarbonate only consider pH <7.0; HHS: slower osmolar correction

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, thrombosis; treatment: hypoglycemia, hypokalemic arrhythmias, cerebral edema (Cushing triad), hyperchloremic acidosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sick-day fluids/ketone checks; continue basal insulin; ensure supplies and early follow-up
Hold SGLT2 inhibitors during acute illness and before surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcoholic ketoacidosis: binge then poor intake; usually no diabetes
Starvation ketosis: usually milder acidosis, no marked hyperglycemia
Toxic alcohols: osmolar gap, exposure; absent substantial ketonemia

table.title: Biochemistry; ketones and HCO₃ in mmol/L

hyperthyroidism.name: Hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis
hyperthyroidism.scope: Graves disease, toxic multinodular goiter, toxic adenoma, subacute thyroiditis, thyroid storm, beta-blockers, thionamides, radioactive iodine
hyperthyroidism.core: Excess circulating thyroid hormone → heat intolerance, weight loss despite appetite, tremor, and tachycardia; hormone overproduction differs from destructive release.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune history, female sex; older age favors autonomous nodules
Iodine load, amiodarone, exogenous thyroid hormone; infection/surgery can precipitate storm

rows.label: Clues
items: Hyperreflexia, lid lag, onycholysis, frequent stools, proximal weakness, widened pulse pressure; older adults: apathetic
★ **Thyroid storm**: fever, delirium, severe tachyarrhythmia, vomiting, heart failure; clinical diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased tissue metabolic activity and beta-adrenergic sensitivity explain systemic manifestations
Thionamides block thyroid peroxidase; PTU also reduces peripheral T4 → T3 conversion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH first → free T4**, total T3 if T4 normal; suppressed TSH with elevated hormones
TRAb establishes Graves; uncertain cause → **Doppler ultrasound** or radioiodine uptake (not if pregnant/lactating)
Low uptake: thyroiditis/exogenous hormone; low thyroglobulin supports exogenous ingestion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptom control: **propranolol**; caution in asthma or decompensated HF
★ Storm → ICU, cooling/fluids, beta-blockade if tolerated, **PTU → iodine ≥1 hour later**, hydrocortisone
Radioiodine contraindicated during pregnancy/lactation; significant active orbitopathy favors another definitive treatment
Compression/suspicious nodule → thyroidectomy after control; pregnancy: first-trimester PTU, later methimazole

rows.label: Complications
items: AF, embolism, osteoporosis, mild hypercalcemia, cardiomyopathy; radioiodine often → hypothyroidism
★ Thionamides: **fever/sore throat → stop drug, urgent CBC**; PTU → severe hepatotoxicity
Pregnancy: thionamides/TRAb cross placenta → **fetal goiter**, impaired swallowing, polyhydramnios

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor free T4 early during treatment; TSH recovery lags
Smoking cessation for orbitopathy; definitive treatment before planned pregnancy when feasible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: episodic symptoms without thyroid biochemical abnormalities
Pheochromocytoma: paroxysmal headache, sweating, severe hypertension
Menopause: hot flashes with menstrual transition, normal thyroid testing
Orbital pseudotumor: involves muscle bellies and tendons; Graves spares tendons

table.title: Etiology determines treatment
rows: Diffuse uptake; bruit, orbitopathy, pretibial myxedema, acropachy (clubbing)
One hot nodule, suppressed surrounding tissue
NSAID; prednisone if severe; no thionamides

hypocalcemia.name: Hypocalcemia
hypocalcemia.scope: Hypoparathyroidism, vitamin D deficiency, post-thyroidectomy, hypomagnesemia
hypocalcemia.core: Low ionized calcium causes neuromuscular irritability and QT prolongation; severe symptoms require IV calcium while the cause is corrected.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Thyroid/parathyroid surgery, autoimmune hypoparathyroidism, DiGeorge syndrome
Vitamin D deficiency from low intake, malabsorption, limited sun; CKD, pancreatitis, massive citrate transfusion
Severe hypomagnesemia from alcoholism, diarrhea, PPIs, diuretics; bisphosphonates/denosumab can precipitate deficiency

rows.label: Clues
items: Perioral tingling, distal paresthesias, muscle cramps, carpopedal spasm
★ **Trousseau sign**: cuff-induced carpal spasm; Chvostek sign is less specific
★ Severe: **seizures, laryngospasm, arrhythmias**; ECG shows prolonged QT
Post-thyroidectomy tingling or stridor requires immediate calcium assessment rather than simple reassurance

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced extracellular calcium lowers nerve excitation threshold; myocardial repolarization is prolonged
Low magnesium impairs both PTH secretion and action, making calcium replacement alone ineffective

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Ionized calcium**, Mg, phosphate, creatinine, PTH, 25-hydroxyvitamin D
Low albumin lowers total calcium, not necessarily ionized; correction formulas unreliable in critical illness
Alkalosis increases albumin binding → symptomatic low ionized calcium despite unchanged total concentration
Interpret PTH relative to calcium: normal PTH can be inappropriately low during hypocalcemia

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptomatic, severe, or ECG changes → **IV calcium gluconate with ECG monitoring**
Mild stable disease → oral calcium; nutritional vitamin D deficiency → cholecalciferol/ergocalciferol
Hypoparathyroidism or advanced CKD → **calcitriol** plus calcium; coordinate phosphate management
★ **Replace magnesium** when deficient; correct underlying cause, avoid overcorrection

rows.label: Complications
items: Tetany, seizures, ventricular arrhythmias; chronic deficiency can cause cataracts and basal ganglia calcification
Overreplacement → hypercalciuria, nephrolithiasis/nephrocalcinosis; monitor serum and urine calcium

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor calcium after neck surgery and antiresorptive treatment; ensure sufficient vitamin D/calcium intake
Chronic hypoparathyroidism: target symptom control with low-normal serum calcium, avoiding renal calcium loading

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hyperventilation syndrome: transient alkalosis-related ionized reduction; assess precipitating illness
Seizure disorder: no biochemical calcium explanation; pseudohypocalcemia: normal ionized level

hypocalcemia.evidence: Not checked online; established endocrine teaching.

hypoglycemia.name: Hypoglycemia
hypoglycemia.scope: Drug-induced hypoglycemia (insulin, sulfonylureas), Whipple triad, acute management (dextrose, glucagon), insulinoma
hypoglycemia.core: Compatible symptoms, documented low plasma glucose, and relief with correction establish Whipple triad and justify evaluation for a hypoglycemic disorder.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Insulin, sulfonylureas; missed meals, exercise, alcohol, kidney failure increase risk
Sepsis, liver failure, adrenal insufficiency; insulinoma causes fasting episodes in otherwise well adults
Child, illness, poor intake or sugar-free fluids → **glycogen depletion**, ketotic hypoglycemia ± anion-gap acidosis

rows.label: Clues
items: Adrenergic: tremor, sweating, palpitations, hunger; neuroglycopenic: confusion, visual change, seizures, coma
Autonomic neuropathy or recurrent episodes may blunt warning symptoms
★ Glucose **<54 mg/dL** clinically significant; diabetes alert threshold <70 mg/dL

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Excess insulin suppresses glucose output and ketones; substrate/hormone deficits impair counterregulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Bedside glucose immediately**; plasma confirmation if discordant, never delay emergency correction
Critical sample: glucose, insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin, β-hydroxybutyrate, sulfonylurea screen
Suspected endogenous fasting disorder → supervised fast up to 72 h; mixed-meal test for postprandial symptoms
Biochemically confirmed insulinoma → pancreatic CT/MRI, endoscopic ultrasound if localization unclear

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Awake and swallowing → **15 g rapid carbohydrate**, recheck after 15 minutes, repeat if needed
★ Altered or unable to swallow → **IV dextrose**; no IV access → IM/intranasal glucagon
After recovery → longer-acting carbohydrate; glucagon less effective after alcohol or glycogen depletion
★ Sulfonylurea recurrence → **octreotide + dextrose**, prolonged observation; long-acting insulin may require infusion
Adjust diabetes regimen and treat trigger; localized insulinoma → surgical resection

rows.label: Complications
items: Seizures, brain injury, arrhythmias, falls; recurrent episodes cause impaired awareness
Dextrose alone after sulfonylurea exposure may stimulate further insulin release

rows.label: Prevention
items: Meal/exercise planning, glucose monitoring or CGM alarms, caregiver rescue-glucagon education
Relax overly intensive targets when recurrent events, frailty, or impaired awareness

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic attack: normal glucose during symptoms
Stroke: focal deficit may persist after glucose correction; evaluate both if unresolved

hypoglycemia.evidence: Not checked online; established endocrine diagnostic and hypoglycemia treatment principles.

hyponatremia.name: Hyponatremia
hyponatremia.scope: Hypovolemic, euvolemic (SIADH, primary polydipsia), hypervolemic, acute vs chronic, hypertonic saline indications
hyponatremia.core: Low serum sodium reflects excess water relative to sodium; symptoms and duration determine urgency before the cause determines maintenance treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Thiazides, SSRIs, carbamazepine/oxcarbazepine, oxytocin; **hypotonic IV D5W**, postoperative state, exercise + excess water
Pulmonary/CNS disease; **small cell lung cancer** (ectopic ADH); heart failure, cirrhosis, renal failure

rows.label: Clues
items: Nausea, headache, gait instability; seizures, coma or marked confusion indicate severe cerebral edema
Orthostasis/dry mucosa suggest depletion; edema/ascites suggest excess extracellular fluid
SIADH: clinically euvolemic with inappropriately concentrated urine despite hypo-osmolality
Massive water intake, often psychiatric illness; urine osmolality below serum still favors polydipsia, even if >100

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hypotonic extracellular fluid drives water into brain; chronic adaptation makes rapid correction dangerous
ADH-mediated water retention or intake exceeding renal dilution capacity lowers sodium concentration
Low effective volume (heart failure, cirrhosis, diarrhea) → baroreceptor ADH release; total-body sodium high in edema

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Serum osmolality first: **<275 mOsm/kg** confirms hypotonicity; assess glucose and volume status
Hyperglycemia → translocational hyponatremia; severe hyperlipidemia/proteinemia → pseudohyponatremia
★ Urine osmolality **<100** → polydipsia/low solute; ≥100 → persistent ADH activity
Urine Na <20–30 suggests low effective arterial volume; >30 suggests renal loss or SIADH
Exclude adrenal insufficiency, hypothyroidism and renal failure before diagnosing SIADH; diuretics confound urine Na

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe neurologic symptoms → **3% saline bolus**, repeated for initial Na rise 4–6 mEq/L
Hypovolemia → isotonic saline; SIADH → fluid restriction, increased solute, remove trigger
Edematous states → fluid/sodium restriction and loop diuretic; treat heart/liver/kidney disorder
★ Chronic/unknown duration: generally limit rise to **≤8 mEq/L per 24 h**; monitor frequently
Overcorrection → desmopressin plus D5W; avoid routine vaptans in acute symptomatic cases

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute severe hyponatremia → herniation, respiratory arrest
Osmotic demyelination after rapid correction; greatest risk with alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid hypotonic maintenance fluids during high ADH states; review causative drugs
Monitor for brisk aquaresis after restoring volume or stopping thiazides

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cerebral salt wasting: neurosurgical patient, hypovolemic, high urine Na; SIADH euvolemic
Hyperosmolar hyperglycemia: measured osmolality elevated
Primary psychiatric disease: neurologic change without sodium abnormality

hyponatremia.evidence: Not checked online; established hyponatremia consensus principles.

hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.name: Hypothesis testing and statistical tests
hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.scope: Null and alternative hypotheses, Type I and Type II errors, statistical power, confidence intervals, p-values, t-tests (paired, unpaired), ANOVA, chi-square, Pearson correlation
hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.core: Hypothesis tests quantify incompatibility with a null model; confidence intervals describe effect estimates and uncertainty.

rows.label: Definition
items: H0: no difference/association; H1: specified difference or association
★ **α**: false-positive probability; Type I error rejects a true null
★ **β**: false-negative probability; Type II error misses a real effect

rows.label: Formula
items: Power = **1 − β**; increases with sample size, effect size, α, lower variability
95% CI ≈ estimate ± 1.96 × standard error; plausible range for true effect

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **p-value**: probability of equally/more extreme data assuming H0; not probability H0 true
95% CI excludes 0 for differences or 1 for ratios → two-sided p <0.05

rows.label: Use when
items: Pearson r: linear association between continuous variables; range −1 to +1
Ordinal/non-normal independent data → Mann–Whitney; paired → Wilcoxon signed-rank

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Nonsignificant ≠ equivalent; statistical significance ≠ clinical importance
Repeated comparisons inflate false positives; prespecify outcomes or adjust α
Correlation neither establishes causation nor detects every nonlinear relationship

hypothesis-testing-and-statistical-tests.evidence: Statistical definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

hypothyroidism.name: Hypothyroidism
hypothyroidism.scope: Hashimoto thyroiditis, subclinical hypothyroidism, myxedema coma, autoimmune associations, levothyroxine dosing, TSH monitoring
hypothyroidism.core: Insufficient thyroid hormone slows metabolism, causing fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, and delayed reflex relaxation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Hashimoto autoimmunity, family history of autoimmune disease; thyroid surgery/radioiodine, iodine deficiency/excess
Lithium, amiodarone, postpartum thyroiditis; pituitary surgery/radiation or mass
Congenital primary → **thyroid dysgenesis** most common, not lymphocytic thyroiditis

rows.label: Clues
items: Weight gain, bradycardia, hoarseness, heavy menses, hyperlipidemia; hyponatremia in severe disease
★ **Hypothermia, altered mentation, hypoventilation, hypotension** → myxedema coma
Autoimmune clustering: type 1 diabetes, pernicious anemia, adrenal insufficiency, celiac disease
Infant: macroglossia, umbilical hernia, prolonged jaundice, hypotonia, large fontanelle → **TSH/free T4**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced hormone activity lowers thermogenesis and cardiac output; glycosaminoglycan deposition produces nonpitting edema
Hashimoto: lymphocytic infiltration; firm painless goiter, even if euthyroid; **anti-TPO/antithyroglobulin** antibodies

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH and free T4** establish hormone deficiency and localize the level of dysfunction
Positive anti-TPO predicts progression from subclinical disease; ultrasound unnecessary without nodule/goiter concern
Recheck mild isolated TSH elevation after transient illness resolves; exclude medication interference

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Levothyroxine**; healthy young adult approximately 1.6 mcg/kg/day; older/CAD start 12.5–25 mcg/day
Fasting, apart from calcium/iron; TSH at 6–8 weeks; **persistently high → increase dose**, even if asymptomatic
Central disease: titrate using free T4; evaluate/replace cortisol before thyroid hormone
Subclinical, untreated: generally start at TSH ≥10; consider symptoms, antibodies, pregnancy at lower values
★ Myxedema: **IV levothyroxine + IV hydrocortisone**, airway support, cautious fluids/passive warming; treat trigger

rows.label: Complications
items: Dyslipidemia, infertility, pericardial effusion, neuropathy; severe disease → respiratory failure
Excess replacement → AF, angina, bone loss; rapid correction in CAD can precipitate ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Pregnancy: early **TSH monitoring**, usually increase existing replacement promptly; use pregnancy-specific targets
Monitor stable replacement at least annually; address adherence/absorption before escalating doses

rows.label: Mimics
items: Depression, dementia, psychosis: normal TSH; hypothyroidism itself can cause reversible cognitive or psychiatric symptoms
Euthyroid sick syndrome: acute systemic illness, often low T3; avoid routine hormone replacement

hypothyroidism.evidence: Not checked online; established thyroid replacement and endocrine emergency teaching.

inflammatory-myopathies.name: Inflammatory myopathies
inflammatory-myopathies.scope: Polymyositis, dermatomyositis, inclusion body myositis, elevated creatine kinase, autoantibodies (anti-Jo-1, anti-Mi-2), muscle biopsy, malignancy screening, systemic corticosteroids
inflammatory-myopathies.core: Objective muscle weakness with elevated muscle enzymes suggests myopathy; distribution, skin findings, and biopsy distinguish treatable inflammation from inclusion body disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune predisposition; adult dermatomyositis associated with occult malignancy
Inclusion body myositis: usually men >50 years; review statin and other myotoxic exposures

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Difficulty rising or lifting arms**, neck flexor weakness; sensation and reflexes generally preserved
Dysphagia, aspiration, dyspnea warrant evaluation for bulbar/respiratory weakness and interstitial lung disease
Dermatomyositis can have characteristic rash before significant muscle weakness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Polymyositis: T-cell-mediated endomysial injury; dermatomyositis: complement-associated microvascular injury
Inclusion body disease combines inflammatory and degenerative pathology, explaining poor immunosuppressive response

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CK, aldolase, AST/ALT**, TSH; muscle can explain transaminase elevation without primary liver disease
Proximal weakness + ↑CK → EMG/nerve conduction (myopathic pattern); MRI guides **muscle biopsy**
★ **Anti-Jo-1**: antisynthetase syndrome with ILD, arthritis, mechanic's hands; **anti-Mi-2**: classic dermatomyositis
Check swallowing and lung function when symptomatic; exclude inherited, endocrine, and drug-induced myopathies

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Polymyositis/dermatomyositis → **systemic glucocorticoids + steroid-sparing agent**, such as methotrexate or azathioprine
Severe/refractory disease or dysphagia → IVIG or other specialist-directed immunomodulation
