pressure-injuries.scope: Stage 1 through 4 pressure injuries, unstageable eschar, risk assessment (Braden scale), pressure offloading, repositioning, wound debridement, dressing selection
pressure-injuries.core: Sustained pressure and shear damage skin and deeper tissue over bony prominences or beneath medical devices.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobility, spinal cord injury, impaired sensation, poor perfusion, malnutrition
Moisture/incontinence, friction, advanced age; oxygen tubing and immobilization devices create focal loading

rows.label: Clues
items: Sacrum, heels, ischial tuberosities, occiput and device contact sites; pain may precede visible injury
Dark skin: assess temperature, induration and discoloration rather than redness alone
Purulence, spreading erythema, fever or worsening pain → infection; exposed bone raises osteomyelitis concern

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Capillary compression and tissue deformation → ischemia/reperfusion damage; shear increases deep injury
Surface appearance may underestimate muscle injury; stages describe depth, not a required progression

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Inspect skin and document depth**, drainage, undermining and surrounding tissue
Braden scale assesses sensory perception, moisture, activity, mobility, nutrition and friction/shear
Suspected osteomyelitis → MRI and, when feasible, bone biopsy/culture; superficial swabs poorly specific
Healing lesions retain their original highest stage; **never reverse-stage**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Offload pressure**, support surfaces and individualized repositioning; float heels with pillows under calves
Saline cleansing; shallow/low-exudate → hydrocolloid; draining → foam/alginate; maintain moisture, protect surrounding skin
★ Necrotic tissue → debridement, except **stable dry heel/ischemic eschar** without infection
Systemic antibiotics only for cellulitis, sepsis or osteomyelitis; not colonization alone
Deep defects → **oral protein/calorie supplements** if malnourished, not parenteral; then negative-pressure, flap closure

rows.label: Complications
items: Cellulitis, osteomyelitis, sepsis, chronic pain and functional decline

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Daily skin checks, mobilization, moisture barriers and adequate protein/calories
Avoid donut cushions, massage over prominences; reassess device fit and risk whenever clinical status changes

rows.label: Mimics
items: Incontinence dermatitis: diffuse superficial moisture-associated damage, not focal loading
Arterial ulcer: distal ischemic site, weak pulses

table.title: Stage by visible depth
rows: Partial thickness; exposed dermis or serum blister
Full thickness; fat visible; no deep structures
Exposed/palpable fascia, muscle, tendon or bone
Persistent maroon/purple discoloration or blood blister

primary-immunodeficiencies.name: Primary immunodeficiencies
primary-immunodeficiencies.scope: Selective IgA deficiency, common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), X-linked agammaglobulinemia, severe combined immunodeficiency, hyper-IgE syndrome, Wiskott-Aldrich, chronic granulomatous disease
primary-immunodeficiencies.core: Recurrent, unusually severe, persistent, or opportunistic infections; organism pattern and age of onset localize the immune defect.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Consanguinity, affected relatives, male relatives dying in infancy; absent family history does not exclude disease

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, persistent thrush, or infections across multiple organ systems
Deep abscesses suggest phagocyte dysfunction; recurrent encapsulated bacteria suggest impaired antibody function

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Selective IgA deficiency: impaired mucosal defense; respiratory infections, giardiasis, atopy, or no symptoms
Antibody disorders impair opsonization; T-cell defects permit viral, fungal, and protozoal opportunists
DiGeorge: 3rd/4th **pharyngeal pouch** failure → absent thymus, hypocalcemia, conotruncal defects, T-cell infections
ADA deficiency: autosomal recessive SCID; toxic deoxyadenosine destroys T and B cells

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Start **CBC with differential, quantitative immunoglobulins**, HIV testing; assess vaccine antibody responses
Lymphocyte subsets distinguish B-cell and T-cell deficiencies; abnormal results → genetic confirmation
IgA deficiency: isolated IgA <7 mg/dL after age 4 years; normal IgG and IgM
★ Newborn **TREC screen** detects impaired T-cell production before symptomatic SCID

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Profound combined immune failure → isolation, irradiated CMV-negative blood products, urgent **transplant evaluation**
Acute infections: organism-directed antimicrobials; immunoglobulin replacement not useful for isolated IgA deficiency

rows.label: Complications
items: Bronchiectasis, chronic enteropathy, autoimmune disease; CVID additionally increases lymphoma risk
Anti-IgA antibodies can cause anaphylaxis to blood products

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Avoid **live vaccines** in major T-cell defects; immunize household contacts with safe vaccine choices
IgA-related transfusion reactions → washed cellular products or IgA-deficient plasma
CGD: TMP-SMX + itraconazole prophylaxis; genetic counseling for inherited defects

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vertical HIV: bacterial infections + zoster, nodes, maternal opportunistic infection; low CD4, positive virologic testing
Secondary hypogammaglobulinemia: nephrotic protein loss, B-cell malignancy, or rituximab exposure

table.title: Defect fingerprints
rows: Adolescent/adult; low IgG, poor vaccine response
Boy after 6 months; absent tonsils/B cells
Infant; absent thymic shadow, profound lymphopenia
Cold abscesses, eczema, retained teeth, pneumatoceles

primary-immunodeficiencies.evidence: Not checked online; established clinical immunology teaching.

renin-angiotensin-system-inhibitors.name: Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors
renin-angiotensin-system-inhibitors.scope: ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, direct renin inhibitors, hyperkalemia, angioedema, cough
renin-angiotensin-system-inhibitors.core: ACE inhibitors, ARBs and aliskiren interrupt the renin–angiotensin–aldosterone axis at different steps.

rows.label: Use
items: ★ **ACE inhibitor or ARB**: hypertension with albuminuric CKD; post-MI ventricular dysfunction
HFrEF: ACE inhibitor/ARB when sacubitril-valsartan cannot be used; aliskiren lacks outcome benefits

rows.label: Mechanism
items: ACE cleaves **C-terminal dipeptide** of angiotensin I → angiotensin II; inhibitors block this step
Efferent arteriolar dilation → ↓glomerular filtration pressure; ↓aldosterone → potassium retention

rows.label: Adverse
items: Hypotension, AKI during hypovolemia; modest stable creatinine rise expected
★ **Angioedema → stop ACE inhibitor permanently**, assess/protect airway; possible even after years

rows.label: Avoid
items: ★ **Pregnancy**, bilateral renal artery stenosis, uncontrolled hyperkalemia
Prior ACE angioedema → no ACE inhibitor; subsequent ARB needs individualized assessment

rows.label: Interactions
items: ★ **Never combine ACE inhibitor, ARB, or aliskiren**; additive kidney injury and hyperkalemia
Potassium supplements, spironolactone, trimethoprim → ↑K; NSAID + diuretic → AKI
Sacubitril-valsartan requires **36-hour ACE inhibitor washout**; RAAS blockade can raise lithium

rows.label: Monitor
items: Baseline BP, creatinine, K → repeat within **2–4 weeks** after initiation/dose increase
Creatinine rise >30% → investigate volume depletion, NSAIDs, renovascular disease; reassess drug

rows.label: Traps
items: Advanced CKD alone → no automatic discontinuation; manage reversible hyperkalemia contributors first

rhabdomyolysis.name: Rhabdomyolysis
rhabdomyolysis.scope: Trauma, crush injury, prolonged immobilization, statins, seizures, elevated CK, myoglobinuria (blood on dipstick without RBCs), acute tubular necrosis, aggressive IV saline hydration
rhabdomyolysis.core: Acute skeletal muscle breakdown releases myoglobin and electrolytes; recognize pigment nephropathy early and restore renal perfusion before kidney failure develops.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: ★ **Crush injury, prolonged immobilization**, compartment syndrome, ischemia/reperfusion
Seizures, strenuous exercise, heatstroke, cocaine; statins, especially with interacting drugs
Hypokalemia, infections, alcohol intoxication; pressure injury during unconsciousness

rows.label: Clues
items: Muscle pain, weakness, swelling; dark urine possible, but classic triad often incomplete
↑K, ↑phosphate, early ↓Ca; AST may rise from muscle rather than liver
Tense painful compartment, pain with passive stretch, sensory change → concurrent limb emergency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Myocyte necrosis → pigment-mediated tubular injury and casts, amplified by hypovolemia and aciduria

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CK >5 times upper limit**, often >1,000 U/L; trend until clearly declining
★ Urine dipstick **heme positive with few/no RBCs** → myoglobin; negative result cannot exclude
Electrolytes, creatinine, ECG, urine output; CK magnitude supports risk assessment, not dialysis alone

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Early **IV normal saline**; titrate to urine output 1–3 mL/kg/hour, avoiding overload
Stop culprit; treat heatstroke/seizures; compartment syndrome → emergency fasciotomy
Hyperkalemic ECG changes → IV calcium, insulin/dextrose; dialysis for refractory electrolyte/volume/acid-base disturbances
★ **No routine bicarbonate or mannitol** for AKI prevention; anuria → reassess fluids, renal consultation
Asymptomatic hypocalcemia → avoid replacement; symptomatic tetany or arrhythmia → calcium

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute tubular necrosis, dangerous arrhythmias, disseminated intravascular coagulation
Recovery phase → rebound hypercalcemia; excessive fluids with renal failure → pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hydration and gradual exercise progression; avoid exertion during severe heat or illness
Review statin interactions, especially macrolides/gemfibrozil; pressure relief during prolonged immobilization

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hematuria: numerous RBCs on microscopy
Hemolysis: heme-positive urine with anemia, ↑LDH, ↓haptoglobin rather than marked CK elevation
Inflammatory myopathy: subacute proximal weakness without acute toxic/traumatic trigger

rhabdomyolysis.evidence: Fluid targets and bicarbonate guidance checked 2026-10-30: [AAST consensus, 2022](https://tsaco.bmj.com/content/7/1/e000836.full.pdf).

routine-prenatal-care.name: Routine prenatal care and early pregnancy
routine-prenatal-care.scope: Pregnancy diagnosis (beta-hCG), initial prenatal assessment, routine first-trimester screening, aneuploidy screening
routine-prenatal-care.core: Confirm and date pregnancy, assess maternal risks, offer one aneuploidy-screening strategy or diagnostic testing, and arrange time-sensitive prenatal studies.

rows.label: Who
items: All pregnancies; review obstetric history, drugs, illness, substance use, violence, family history
Offer carrier screening and genetic counseling; discuss patient preferences and right to decline

rows.label: Start/stop
items: Early visit: urine hCG confirms pregnancy; serum quantitative hCG for uncertain/complicated cases
★ First-trimester **ultrasound crown–rump length** best establishes gestational age
Serum screen 10–13 6/7 weeks; NT 11–13 6/7; cfDNA from 10 weeks

rows.label: Test
items: ★ Initial **CBC, ABO/Rh, antibody screen, urine culture**; HIV, syphilis, HBsAg, HCV, rubella immunity
GC/chlamydia by age/risk; offer one aneuploidy strategy regardless of maternal age
Anatomy ultrasound 18–22 weeks; AFP for open neural tube defects when not otherwise assessed

rows.label: IF positive
items: ★ Abnormal screen → counseling, ultrasound, **CVS/amniocentesis** before irreversible decisions
CVS: 10–13 weeks; amniocentesis: ≥15 weeks; neither automatically required after negative screening
Rh-negative, unsensitized → anti-D prophylaxis at 28 weeks and after sensitizing events

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **cfDNA is screening**, not diagnostic; does not screen open neural tube defects
Single hCG value cannot establish viability or location; pain/bleeding → ectopic evaluation
Folate before conception/early gestation; avoid alcohol, tobacco, teratogens; no live vaccines

table.title: Early and routine pregnancy calls
rows: Nausea, irregular bleeding or amenorrhea, even premenarche
Missed menses, urinary frequency, friable cervix, enlarged uterus
Brief sharp movement-triggered lower-quadrant pain, normal vitals
No added preterm, fluid, or placental risk

scrotal-masses.name: Scrotal masses
scrotal-masses.scope: Varicocele, hydrocele, spermatocele, testicular cancer differential, physical examination, scrotal Doppler ultrasound
scrotal-masses.core: Painless scrotal swelling requires localization: solid intratesticular lesions are malignant until proven otherwise; many extratesticular lesions are benign.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Testicular cancer: cryptorchidism, prior cancer, family history, younger adult age
Hydrocele: infancy/patent processus vaginalis, trauma, infection; varicocele from venous drainage anatomy

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Firm nontransilluminating intratesticular mass** → urgent malignancy assessment
Dull ache/heaviness may occur without acute inflammation; gynecomastia suggests hormone-secreting germ-cell tumor
New isolated right-sided varicocele or failure to decompress supine → evaluate retroperitoneal obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Patent processus vaginalis permits peritoneal-scrotal communication; epididymal duct obstruction forms retention cysts
Pampiniform venous reflux raises local temperature, potentially impairing spermatogenesis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Nonclassic or possibly solid mass → **scrotal Doppler ultrasound**: intra-/extratesticular location, blood flow
Classic left varicocele on examination → clinical diagnosis; **no imaging**
Examine standing/supine, with Valsalva; determine whether testis separately palpable and mass transilluminates
Suspected tumor → AFP, beta-hCG, LDH before surgery; staging CT chest/abdomen/pelvis as needed
Normal markers do not exclude malignancy; AFP elevation excludes pure seminoma

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspicious testicular mass → **radical inguinal orchiectomy**; avoid transscrotal biopsy
Offer sperm banking before cancer treatment; subsequent surveillance/chemotherapy/radiation depends on histology/stage
Newborn transilluminating hydrocele → routine follow-up, usually resolves within 12 months; no aspiration or imaging
Small asymptomatic hydrocele/spermatocele → observe; persistent symptomatic → elective repair
★ Varicocele with **infertility and abnormal semen**, pain, or adolescent testicular atrophy → consider repair

rows.label: Complications
items: Infertility, testicular atrophy; cancer metastasis to retroperitoneal nodes/lungs
Hydrocele may obscure tumor; treatment can impair fertility or endocrine function

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Orchiopexy for undescended testis** reduces infertility risk and facilitates examination; cancer risk persists
No routine population ultrasound or tumor-marker screening; promptly evaluate any new mass

rows.label: Mimics
items: Torsion: sudden severe pain, high-riding testis, absent cremasteric reflex → urgent exploration
Inguinal hernia: reducible groin-continuous swelling, cough impulse
Epididymitis: tender posterior swelling, urinary/STI findings, increased Doppler flow

table.title: Benign examination patterns
rows: Bag of worms; enlarges standing/Valsalva, decompresses supine
Cyst above/behind testis; separate, often transilluminates

scrotal-masses.evidence: Not checked online; established urologic localization and cancer-evaluation principles.

septic-arthritis.name: Septic arthritis
septic-arthritis.scope: Nongonococcal, gonococcal, prosthetic joint infection, IV drug use, empiric coverage (vancomycin + cefepime), contiguous osteomyelitis
septic-arthritis.core: Acutely painful swollen joint with restricted passive motion → urgent aspiration and drainage; delayed treatment rapidly destroys cartilage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthesis, recent surgery/injection, rheumatoid arthritis, immunosuppression, diabetes, bacteremia
IV drug use → S aureus and gram-negative risk, including Pseudomonas
Young sexually active adults → disseminated gonorrhea; adjacent ulcers/osteomyelitis → contiguous spread
RA joint with new febrile monoarthritis → infection until aspirated, not flare

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually acute monoarthritis, often knee; fever may be absent, especially in older/immunocompromised adults
★ **Severe pain with both active and passive motion**; inability to bear weight; child's hip held flexed, abducted, externally rotated
Gonococcal dissemination: migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules; may progress to purulent monoarthritis
Prosthetic infection: persistent pain, loosening, wound drainage or sinus tract, sometimes minimal systemic illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Hematogenous seeding or direct inoculation → neutrophilic enzymes damage articular cartilage
Implant biofilm limits antibiotic eradication without surgical source control
★ **S aureus** most common, including RA-damaged joints: gram-positive cocci in clusters
Asplenia or recent pharyngitis → **streptococci**: gram-positive cocci in chains

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Arthrocentesis before antibiotics** when stable: cell count/differential, Gram stain, culture, crystals
Synovial WBC >50,000/µL, neutrophil predominance supports infection; lower counts or negative Gram stain never exclude
★ **Crystals do not exclude infection**; send cultures even when gout seems likely
Blood cultures; gonococcal: aspirate on **chocolate/Thayer-Martin agar** plus mucosal NAAT; MRI for suspected contiguous osteomyelitis
New warmth/effusion in OA joint → aspirate before any intra-articular steroid

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ After cultures → **IV vancomycin + cefepime or piperacillin-tazobactam** for severe disease, IV drug use, gram-negative risk
Stable low-risk adult: vancomycin ± ceftriaxone based on exposure; narrow to organism/susceptibility
Sepsis → immediate antibiotics without delaying for aspiration; large joints: arthroscopic washout; **hip → operative drainage**, not serial aspiration
Persistent symptoms → repeat drainage, seek abscess/osteomyelitis; mobilize after infection controlled

rows.label: Complications
items: Irreversible joint destruction, avascular necrosis, osteomyelitis, bacteremia, sepsis
Prolonged antibiotics → renal injury, line complications, C difficile; prolonged immobility → stiffness

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sterile procedures, treat skin infections, injection-harm reduction
Gonorrhea: treat partners, screen other STIs, abstain until treatment completed and partners treated

rows.label: Mimics
items: Crystal arthritis: polarized crystals; infection still possible concurrently
Bursitis: localized periarticular swelling, passive joint motion relatively preserved
Reactive arthritis: sterile inflammatory arthritis after GI/GU infection
Transient synovitis (child): afebrile, bears weight, ESR <40, WBC <12,000

table.title: Special treatment branches
rows: Debridement, implant retention, prolonged pathogen-directed antibiotics

skin-cancer.name: Skin cancer
skin-cancer.scope: Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, melanoma, photoprotection and sunscreen
skin-cancer.core: Changing pigmented lesions or persistent keratinizing, pearly, or ulcerated growths require examination and tissue diagnosis rather than empiric reassurance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: UV exposure, fair skin, sunburns, tanning beds, older age; immunosuppression particularly increases SCC
Melanoma: numerous/atypical nevi, family/personal melanoma history; may arise without a preexisting nevus
Chronic wounds/scars predispose SCC; acral melanoma occurs regardless of skin pigmentation

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Melanoma: **ABCDE**—asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, evolution; ugly-duckling lesion
Diameter >6 mm concerning, but smaller evolving lesions still require biopsy
Amelanotic melanoma may be pink; inspect soles, palms, nail beds; nail pigment extending onto fold concerning
Rapid growth, bleeding, nonhealing ulcer, fixation, neurologic symptoms, nodes → aggressive or advanced disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: UV-induced DNA damage → keratinocyte malignancy; melanocyte transformation causes melanoma
AK represents dysplastic keratinocytes with potential progression to invasive SCC

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious melanoma → **full-thickness excisional biopsy with narrow margins** to measure Breslow depth
Partial biopsy acceptable when complete excision impractical; avoid superficial sampling that prevents staging
Suspected keratinocyte carcinoma → deep shave or punch biopsy; <1 cm → **narrow-margin excisional biopsy**
AK persisting after topical fluorouracil → **excisional biopsy** to exclude invasive SCC
Breslow thickness/ulceration guide melanoma staging; sentinel-node discussion generally at ≥0.8 mm or ulceration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive cancers → **surgical excision**; high-risk/recurrent facial BCC/SCC → Mohs
Low-risk BCC → **excision with narrow margins (≤1 cm)**; no sentinel node biopsy
Positive margin on BCC/SCC → **reexcision** or Mohs, not observation
★ Melanoma → **wide local excision after diagnostic biopsy**; margins depend on depth
Advanced melanoma → specialist immunotherapy, selected BRAF-targeted drugs; avoid destructive treatment before diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: BCC: extensive local destruction, rare metastasis; SCC: nodal metastasis, especially high-risk sites/immunosuppression
Melanoma: distant metastases, including brain; immunotherapy → colitis, endocrinopathies, pneumonitis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Broad-spectrum SPF ≥30**, reapply every 2 hours/outdoors after swimming; shade, protective clothing, no tanning
Infants <6 months → **shade, protective clothing**; avoid sunscreen
Self-examination, postcancer follow-up; suspicious lesions require evaluation despite uncertain population-screening benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seborrheic keratosis: waxy stuck-on plaque; atypical lesions still biopsy
Dermatofibroma: firm papule with dimple sign
Benign nevus: stable symmetric uniform, <6 mm → **observation**, even with melanoma family history
Congenital melanocytic nevus: brown lesion from birth, may darken or grow coarse hair

table.title: Nonmelanoma patterns
rows: Nonhealing scaly indurated plaque/ulcer/nodule; lip/ear common
Assess high-risk features and regional nodes
Pearly rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulcer
Treat despite slow growth; local invasion

skin-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAD melanoma guidance](https://www.aad.org/member/clinical-quality/guidelines/melanoma); established keratinocyte-cancer and photoprotection teaching.

solid-organ-transplantation.name: Solid organ transplantation
solid-organ-transplantation.scope: Hyperacute rejection, acute allograft rejection, chronic allograft rejection, immunosuppressive regimens
solid-organ-transplantation.core: Allograft dysfunction requires urgent distinction among rejection, infection, obstruction/vascular failure, and immunosuppressant toxicity; biopsy usually establishes the rejection mechanism.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HLA mismatch; sensitization after transplant, transfusion or pregnancy → preformed donor-specific antibodies
Missed immunosuppression, underdosing, drug interactions; rejection can occur late after medication withdrawal

rows.label: Clues
items: Kidney: ↑creatinine; liver: ↑bilirubin/enzymes; heart: ventricular dysfunction; lung: ↓spirometry
Fever, graft tenderness or malaise possible; rejection may be asymptomatic before laboratory abnormalities

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Allorecognition targets donor tissue; immunosuppression balances graft protection against infection and malignancy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Graft ultrasound/Doppler** when relevant → exclude obstruction, thrombosis or vascular compromise
Medication adherence/troughs, cultures and organ-specific viral testing; donor-specific antibodies assess humoral injury
★ **Allograft biopsy** distinguishes rejection from drug toxicity/infection; C4d may support antibody-mediated injury

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Common kidney maintenance: **tacrolimus + mycophenolate ± prednisone**; regimen varies by organ and risk
Induction in selected recipients → basiliximab or antithymocyte globulin
Steroid-resistant cellular rejection → antithymocyte globulin; coordinate all treatment with transplant team
Never reflexively escalate immunosuppression for unexplained fever before evaluating infection

rows.label: Complications
items: Calcineurin inhibitors → nephrotoxicity, hypertension, neurotoxicity; tacrolimus → diabetes
Mycophenolate → cytopenias, diarrhea, teratogenicity; sirolimus → poor wound healing, hyperlipidemia
Glucocorticoids → diabetes/osteoporosis; immunosuppression → opportunistic infection, skin cancer, EBV-related PTLD

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **ABO compatibility, HLA assessment, crossmatch** before transplant; lifelong adherence and trough monitoring
TMP-SMX prophylaxis for Pneumocystis; valganciclovir or preemptive monitoring for CMV according to risk
Vaccinate before transplant; avoid live vaccines during immunosuppression; sun protection and skin checks

rows.label: Mimics
items: Calcineurin toxicity: excessive exposure, no graft tenderness/enlargement; compatible biopsy, no alloimmune infiltrates
BK nephropathy: kidney transplant, viral PCR and viral inclusions on biopsy
Mechanical graft failure: obstruction/thrombosis demonstrated by imaging

table.title: Rejection patterns
rows: T-cell infiltrates; liver: portal eosinophils, endotheliitis

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.name: Stable ischemic heart disease
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.scope: Stable angina pectoris, exercise stress testing, stress echocardiography, antianginal pharmacotherapy, invasive coronary angiography indications
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.core: Predictable exertional chest pressure relieved by rest reflects myocardial oxygen supply–demand mismatch; new rest symptoms require acute coronary syndrome evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, older age, family history of premature CAD
Anemia, tachycardia, and uncontrolled blood pressure can worsen ischemic symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Substernal squeezing, arm/jaw radiation; dyspnea or exertional indigestion may be anginal equivalents
Normal resting ECG does not exclude CAD; examination often normal between episodes
★ **Crescendo symptoms, prolonged pain, rest pain**, instability → ECG/troponins and ACS pathway

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Flow-limiting coronary atherosclerosis restricts supply when demand rises
Microvascular dysfunction can produce ischemia despite absence of obstructive epicardial disease

rows.label: Dx
items: Resting ECG, lipid profile, HbA1c, renal function; estimate clinical likelihood before choosing testing
★ Selected intermediate-risk suspected CAD → **CCTA or stress testing**, based on suitability
★ **Coronary angiography** for high-risk noninvasive findings, refractory limiting symptoms, or suspected high-risk anatomy
Stable on medical therapy, low-risk ischemia → no repeat testing or mandatory catheterization; respect informed refusal
Sedentary, risk factors, starting vigorous exercise: no routine stress test; older exam questions may expect exercise ECG

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Relief → **sublingual nitroglycerin**; avoid with recent PDE-5 inhibitor use or hypotension
★ Prevention → **aspirin + high-intensity statin**; manage BP/diabetes, lifestyle and exercise
Antianginal first-line: beta blocker or calcium-channel blocker; persistent symptoms → long-acting nitrate or ranolazine
Beta blockers improve outcomes for selected recent MI/reduced EF indications, not all stable CAD indefinitely
Refractory symptoms → revascularization; CABG improves survival in left-main/selected complex multivessel disease

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, heart failure, malignant arrhythmia, sudden death
Nitrates → headache/hypotension; combining beta blocker with verapamil/diltiazem can cause bradycardia/heart block

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, Mediterranean-style diet, habitual activity; cardiac rehabilitation when eligible
ACE inhibitor/ARB when hypertension, diabetes, CKD, or reduced EF; adherence and lipid follow-up
Drug-eluting stent → **aspirin + clopidogrel**, not anticoagulant; stable CAD 6 months; older exam questions may expect 12

rows.label: Mimics
items: GERD: meal/recumbency association, regurgitation
Aortic stenosis: exertional symptoms with systolic murmur
Costochondritis: reproducible focal chest-wall tenderness
Variant (Prinzmetal) vasospasm: rest/nocturnal pain, **transient ST elevation**, nitrate relief, normal angiography → calcium-channel blocker

table.title: Functional test selection
rows: Exercise stress echocardiography or perfusion imaging

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC chronic coronary disease guideline summary (2023)](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2023/07/17/19/06/2023-guideline-for-chronic-coronary-disease-gl-ccd/).

stevens-johnson-syndrome.name: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
stevens-johnson-syndrome.scope: SJS and TEN (<10% vs >30% BSA detachment), culprit drugs (antibiotics, anticonvulsants, allopurinol), mucosal involvement, Nikolsky sign, burn unit management
stevens-johnson-syndrome.core: Recent medication exposure, fever, and rapidly spreading tender dusky macules; epidermal necrolysis severity follows detached surface area.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Usually 1–4 weeks after starting sulfonamides/antibiotics, lamotrigine, carbamazepine, phenytoin, allopurinol, NSAIDs
Previous reaction, HIV; risk modified by drug-specific HLA susceptibility

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Painful erosions, ≥2 mucosal sites (oral, ocular, genital)**; flat atypical targets, flaccid bullae, sheet-like sloughing
★ **Nikolsky sign**: epidermis shears with gentle lateral pressure; not specific to SJS/TEN
Dysphonia, secretion intolerance, hypoxemia → airway involvement; tachycardia/hypotension → systemic deterioration

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Drug-triggered cytotoxic T cells/NK cells release granulysin and related mediators → widespread keratinocyte apoptosis

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Clinical emergency; **skin biopsy** confirms full-thickness epidermal necrosis and subepidermal separation
Count detached/detachable skin, not total erythematous area; document every mucosal site
CBC, electrolytes, creatinine, bicarbonate, glucose, LFTs; cultures for suspected infection; SCORTEN estimates mortality

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Stop culprit/nonessential drugs immediately**; urgent dermatology, burn/ICU assessment; extensive loss → specialized unit
Airway assessment, IV crystalloid titrated to perfusion, electrolyte replacement, warming, analgesia, early enteral nutrition
Nonadherent wound care, minimize skin trauma; **urgent ophthalmology** for lubrication and ocular-surface protection
Systemic antibiotics only for clinical infection; no routine prophylaxis or routine thermal-burn fluid formulas
Cyclosporine/etanercept or other immunomodulation: specialist decision; no universal regimen; never delay supportive care

rows.label: Complications
items: Sepsis, fluid/electrolyte losses, AKI, respiratory failure, death; risk increases with greater epidermal loss
Corneal scarring/blindness, symblepharon, genital/urinary strictures, pigment/nail changes, psychological sequelae

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Document **permanent culprit avoidance**, related-drug review, medical alert identification; never diagnostic rechallenge
Carbamazepine, at-risk Asian ancestry → HLA-B*15:02 screening; positive → choose alternative
Allopurinol: HLA-B*58:01 screening for African American, Han Chinese, Korean, Thai ancestry

rows.label: Mimics
items: Staphylococcal scalded skin: infants, superficial cleavage, mucosa spared
Erythema multiforme: raised classic targets, acral distribution, often HSV-triggered
DRESS: eosinophilia, facial edema, hepatitis; usually no extensive epidermal detachment
Kawasaki disease: ≥5 days fever, nonexudative conjunctivitis, strawberry tongue; no mucosal erosions or culprit drug

study-designs.name: Study designs
study-designs.scope: Case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, RCT, control selection, bias, internal and external validity
study-designs.core: Study design determines how participants are selected, when exposure/outcome are measured, and which associations can be estimated without avoidable bias.

rows.label: Definition
items: Internal validity: credible within-study inference; external validity: applicability elsewhere
**Selection/ascertainment bias**: institutional or already-ill sample misrepresents target population
Subjective scoring by different raters → **interobserver variability**; standardize criteria

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Randomization balances confounders on average**; concealed allocation prevents enrollment bias
Blinding reduces behavior/assessment bias; intention-to-treat retains original randomized groups
Loss to follow-up can bias estimates when related to exposure and outcome

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Case-control controls → **same source population** that produced cases, independent of exposure
Prospective measurement improves temporality but does not eliminate confounding in observational research
Life table: poorest 1-year survival → steepest interval drop, not lowest cumulative point

rows.label: Compare
items: Confounding: third-variable distortion; randomize, restrict, match, stratify, or adjust
Effect modification: association differs across strata; report rather than remove it
Clinician-chosen treatment → **selection bias/confounding by indication**; randomization prevents it

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Case-control sampling cannot directly estimate incidence or risk** without additional population data
★ Cross-sectional data lack reliable **temporal sequence**; prevalent cases favor longer survivors
Random selection supports generalizability; random assignment supports causal inference

study-designs.evidence: Established epidemiologic definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

subarachnoid-hemorrhage.name: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
subarachnoid-hemorrhage.scope: Ruptured saccular aneurysm, thunderclap headache, noncontrast head CT, lumbar puncture and xanthochromia, nimodipine, complications
subarachnoid-hemorrhage.core: Sudden headache maximal within seconds, often during exertion, with possible meningismus or collapse: presume subarachnoid hemorrhage until excluded.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, hypertension, family history, prior aneurysm; autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
**Saccular aneurysm rupture**: most common nontraumatic cause, exceeds AVM; circle-of-Willis branch points; cocaine ↑ risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Vomiting, photophobia, neck stiffness, transient loss of consciousness; sentinel headache may precede major hemorrhage
★ **Painful pupil-involving CN III palsy** → posterior communicating artery aneurysm
Sudden stupor, focal deficits, Cushing response, seizures → raised ICP/herniation; normal exam does not exclude hemorrhage

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Blood enters subarachnoid space → meningeal irritation, ↑ICP, impaired CSF resorption
Blood-breakdown products and vascular injury contribute to delayed cerebral ischemia

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Noncontrast head CT immediately**: hyperdense basal cisterns/sulci; sensitivity declines with elapsed time
★ Negative CT >6 hours after onset or neurologic deficit → **LP**, assessing xanthochromia and RBCs
High-quality CT within 6 hours, neurologically intact, expert interpretation → may exclude SAH without routine LP
Confirmed blood → **CT angiography**; negative/inconclusive CTA with suspected aneurysm → catheter angiography
Traumatic tap may show falling RBCs; clearing alone cannot reliably exclude SAH

rows.label: Tx
items: Support airway, reverse anticoagulation, analgesia; severe hypertension → IV nicardipine; avoid hypotension/BP swings
★ **Urgent aneurysm coiling or clipping**, preferably within 24 hours, prevents rebleeding
★ **Enteral nimodipine for 21 days**, maintain euvolemia; no prophylactic hypervolemia
Acute symptomatic hydrocephalus → external ventricular drainage
Secured aneurysm + delayed ischemia → induced hypertension; refractory → endovascular vasodilator/angioplasty

rows.label: Complications
items: Early rebleeding, hydrocephalus, seizures; delayed ischemia typically days 3–14
Hyponatremia from SIADH or cerebral salt wasting; stress cardiomyopathy, arrhythmias, pulmonary edema
ACom aneurysm rupture/clipping → **frontal lobe injury**: abulia, apathy, reduced spontaneous speech without depressed mood

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation and BP control; specialist screening discussion for ≥2 affected first-degree relatives or high-risk ADPKD

rows.label: Mimics
items: Reversible cerebral vasoconstriction: recurrent thunderclap headaches; segmental angiographic narrowing
Meningitis: fever and inflammatory CSF rather than aneurysmal bleeding
Migraine: usually slower onset, recurrent stereotyped episodes; first thunderclap still needs hemorrhage evaluation

syncope.name: Syncope
syncope.scope: Vasovagal / neurocardiogenic syncope, orthostatic syncope, situational syncope, cardiogenic syncope, breath-holding spells, cerebral hypoperfusion workup
syncope.core: Brief loss of consciousness from global cerebral hypoperfusion with rapid spontaneous recovery; identify cardiac danger before labeling an episode reflex-mediated.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Dehydration, blood loss, autonomic dysfunction, diuretics, nitrates, alpha-1 blockers; prolonged standing, heat, fear
Structural heart disease, conduction disease, arrhythmias, family history of sudden death

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Exertional or supine syncope**, palpitations, absent prodrome, cardiac murmur → high-risk cause
Reflex prodrome: nausea, warmth, diaphoresis, tunnel vision; may include brief myoclonic jerks
Situational triggers: urination, coughing, defecation; breath-holding spells follow crying/pain in young children
Shaving, tight collar, head turning + bradycardia → **carotid sinus hypersensitivity**; confirm with carotid sinus massage

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Vasodilation/bradycardia, failed postural compensation, or low cardiac output transiently limits cerebral flow

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Initial **history, examination, orthostatic BP, ECG**; bedside glucose and targeted pregnancy/bleeding evaluation
Orthostasis: systolic fall ≥20 or diastolic ≥10 mm Hg within 3 minutes standing
High-risk → admission/monitoring; suspected structural disease → echo; intermittent arrhythmia → ambulatory ECG
Tilt-table testing for recurrent unexplained reflex/orthostatic cases; no routine head CT, EEG, carotid ultrasound
Typical breath-holding spells: normal development, awake trigger, rapid recovery; CBC/ferritin and ECG when evaluating

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Reflex event → supine, legs elevated; **hydration, counterpressure maneuvers**, trigger recognition
Orthostatic cause → replace volume, review drugs, rise slowly, compression; refractory neurogenic cases → midodrine
★ Cardiac cause → **treat rhythm/obstruction**, restrict unsafe activity pending evaluation
Breath-holding: reassure caregivers, safe positioning, treat iron deficiency; no antiseizure drugs

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, fractures, driving injury; underlying cardiac disease carries sudden-death risk
Recurrent episodes → activity limitation, anxiety; pressor drugs can cause supine hypertension

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid dehydration and prolonged immobility; individualized driving/activity restrictions after unexplained or cardiac events

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seizure: prolonged postictal confusion, lateral tongue biting; incontinence occurs in both
Hypoglycemia: persistent altered state until glucose corrected
TIA: focal deficit; isolated transient unconsciousness unusual

syncope.evidence: Not checked online; established syncope evaluation teaching.

systemic-lupus-erythematosus.name: Systemic lupus erythematosus
systemic-lupus-erythematosus.scope: Diagnostic criteria (serositis, arthritis, lupus nephritis), neonatal lupus (congenital AV block), autoantibodies (ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith), pharmacotherapy (hydroxychloroquine, glucocorticoids)
systemic-lupus-erythematosus.core: Multisystem autoimmunity combining inflammatory joint, skin, serosal, renal, hematologic, or neurologic disease; flares often lower complement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Reproductive-age women; family history; UV exposure, infections, estrogen-related triggers

rows.label: Clues
items: Photosensitive malar rash sparing nasolabial folds; painless oral ulcers; nonscarring alopecia
Symmetric nonerosive arthritis, pleuritic pain, pericarditis; leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, hemolysis
★ **Proteinuria, RBC casts**, edema or hypertension → renal involvement
Neonatal lupus: maternal anti-Ro/SSA or anti-La/SSB; congenital AV block may be permanent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Immune-complex deposition activates **classical complement**, consuming C3/C4; autoantibody-mediated blood-cell destruction

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ANA** sensitive entry test; anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm more specific
Anti-dsDNA titers, C3/C4, CBC, urinalysis, urine protein/creatinine, creatinine assess activity
★ Proteinuria **>0.5 g/g** or unexplained renal dysfunction → kidney biopsy
Classification: ANA ≥1:80, weighted score ≥10 with clinical criterion; clinical diagnosis remains contextual

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Hydroxychloroquine** broadly; NSAIDs for mild arthritis/serositis, glucocorticoids for flares
Organ-threatening flare → IV methylprednisolone; nephritis → mycophenolate plus belimumab/calcineurin inhibitor
Cyclophosphamide alternative for severe renal/CNS disease; taper glucocorticoids after disease control
Pregnancy → continue hydroxychloroquine; avoid mycophenolate, methotrexate, cyclophosphamide

rows.label: Complications
items: Accelerated atherosclerosis, infection, CKD; antiphospholipid antibodies → thrombosis or pregnancy loss
Hydroxychloroquine retinal toxicity; chronic steroid osteoporosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Sun protection; vaccines, cardiovascular risk control, retinal monitoring
Plan pregnancy during quiescence; anti-Ro/La positivity → fetal cardiac surveillance discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Drug-induced lupus: antihistone antibodies, usually no renal/CNS disease
Rheumatoid arthritis: erosions; fibromyalgia: pain without inflammatory findings

systemic-vasculitis.name: Systemic vasculitis
systemic-vasculitis.scope: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (c-ANCA/PR3), microscopic polyangiitis (p-ANCA/MPO), eosinophilic GPA, polyarteritis nodosa, giant cell arteritis, Takayasu arteritis, immunosuppressive therapy
systemic-vasculitis.core: Vessel inflammation presenting as unexplained multisystem ischemia: vessel size, organ pattern, antibodies and tissue distinguish the syndromes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune predisposition; hydralazine/propylthiouracil can induce ANCA disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Constitutional symptoms, palpable purpura, skin ulcers, mononeuritis multiplex
★ **Hemoptysis + falling hemoglobin + RBC casts** → pulmonary–renal emergency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ANCA disease → pauci-immune necrotizing injury; larger-vessel inflammation → stenosis, thrombosis, aneurysms
Granulomas: GPA/EGPA, GCA/Takayasu; PAN: necrotizing medium-artery inflammation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis, creatinine, CBC/differential, ESR/CRP**, chest imaging, hepatitis serologies
PR3/MPO supports diagnosis; negative ANCA cannot exclude, isolated positive cannot confirm
★ **Biopsy involved tissue**, especially kidney with GN; do not delay emergency therapy
GCA → temporal artery biopsy/expert ultrasound; **steroids before confirmation**
Takayasu → CTA/MRA; PAN → biopsy or visceral angiography showing microaneurysms

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Organ-threatening disease → **urgent immunosuppression**; stabilize bleeding, renal failure, ischemia
GPA/MPA maintenance → rituximab/azathioprine; methotrexate if renal function permits
Plasma exchange not routine in ANCA; consider severe renal disease/anti-GBM overlap
GCA steroid sparing → tocilizumab; elective vascular reconstruction after inflammation controlled
HCV cryoglobulinemia → **direct-acting antivirals**, not immunosuppression alone; older questions may expect interferon-alfa

rows.label: Complications
items: Blindness, renal failure, stroke, bowel infarction, aortic aneurysm
Cyclophosphamide → infertility/cystitis/malignancy; rituximab → HBV reactivation; steroids → infection/osteoporosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **TMP-SMX** with cyclophosphamide/rituximab induction; HBV/TB testing before biologics
Vaccination, bone protection, fertility counseling; follow clinical findings, not ANCA titers alone

rows.label: Mimics
items: Endocarditis: positive blood cultures/vegetations; ANCA sometimes positive
Anti-GBM: linear IgG on renal biopsy
Cholesterol emboli: vascular procedure, blue toes, eosinophilia, preserved pulses

table.title: Disease signatures
rows: PR3/c-ANCA; destructive sinonasal/ear disease, cavitary lungs, GN
Severe disease: same induction as GPA
Steroids; severe → cyclophosphamide; nonsevere relapsing → mepolizumab
Age >50; jaw claudication, visual symptoms, PMR
Young women; pulse/BP discrepancy, arm claudication

thoracic-trauma.name: Thoracic trauma
thoracic-trauma.scope: Blunt and penetrating chest trauma, blunt cardiac injury, blunt aortic injury, diaphragmatic rupture, pulmonary contusion
thoracic-trauma.core: Chest trauma with respiratory or circulatory compromise requires immediate treatment of life-threatening injuries before definitive imaging.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: High-speed deceleration, steering-wheel impact, crush injuries, penetrating wounds
Lower chest wounds can cross diaphragm and injure abdominal organs

rows.label: Clues
items: Unilateral absent breath sounds, shock, distended neck veins → tension pneumothorax
Flail segment: paradoxical movement; associated lung injury drives hypoxemia
Hypoxemia hours after impact + focal alveolar infiltrate, worsening to 24–48 h, afebrile → **pulmonary contusion**
Left thoracic bowel sounds/loops, **NG tip in left chest**, obscured hemidiaphragm → diaphragmatic rupture

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pleural pressure or pericardial blood impairs venous return → obstructive shock
Alveolar hemorrhage and edema impair gas exchange; rapid deceleration shears the aortic isthmus

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Primary survey with **eFAST** and portable chest radiograph; unstable injuries treated clinically
★ Deceleration + **widened mediastinum** → aortic injury; stable → **CT angiography**; normal radiograph cannot exclude
Blunt cardiac injury → ECG and troponin; both normal effectively exclude significant injury
Sternal/anterior rib fractures + new arrhythmia/↑troponin → telemetry; persistent shock → echocardiography
Large persistent air leak, subcutaneous air despite working chest tube → **tracheobronchial rupture**; bronchoscopy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tension pneumothorax → immediate needle/finger decompression → **chest tube**; no imaging delay
Open pneumothorax → vented seal and tube; hemothorax → tube and blood resuscitation
★ Initial tube blood >1500 mL or persistent >200 mL/h → operative exploration
Tamponade with shock/arrest → surgical drainage; pericardiocentesis only temporizing
Contusion/flail chest → oxygen, regional/multimodal analgesia, pulmonary hygiene; intubate for respiratory failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Contusion → ARDS; retained hemothorax → empyema
Rib fractures → splinting, atelectasis, pneumonia; cardiac injury → arrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Seat belts, vehicle safety systems and protective equipment reduce injury risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Myocardial contusion: ventricular ectopy, rising wedge pressure, pulmonary edema after fluids; no pericardial compression
Abdominal hemorrhage: free intraperitoneal fluid; may coexist with thoracic injury
Massive hemothorax: **opacified hemithorax**, flat neck veins; tension pneumothorax: hyperlucent
ARDS: bilateral opacities after 24–48 h; fat embolism: long-bone fracture, petechiae, confusion

thoracic-trauma.evidence: Not checked online; established ATLS-based teaching.

table.title: Definitive associated-injury management
rows: IV esmolol if tolerated; endovascular repair

thrombocytopenia.name: Thrombocytopenia
thrombocytopenia.scope: Evaluation of isolated thrombocytopenia, peripheral smear, immune thrombocytopenia, drug-induced, procedural platelet thresholds
thrombocytopenia.core: Low platelet count requires confirmation and distinction among impaired production, immune destruction, consumption, sequestration, and laboratory artifact.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Recent infection, autoimmune disease, HIV/HCV, lymphoproliferative disease → secondary immune thrombocytopenia
Heparin, quinine, TMP-SMX, vancomycin; alcohol, marrow-suppressive drugs; cirrhosis with splenic sequestration

rows.label: Clues
items: Petechiae, purpura, epistaxis, gingival bleeding; mucosal hemorrhage signals clinically important platelet disorder
★ **Neurologic/renal abnormalities + hemolysis** → thrombotic microangiopathy; systemic illness/coagulopathy → DIC
Heparin exposure + >50% platelet decline, thrombosis, typical 5–10-day onset → HIT

rows.label: Pathophys
items: ITP: IgG platelet clearance, impaired megakaryocytes; maternal IgG crosses placenta → **fetal platelet destruction**
Drug-dependent immune destruction often causes abrupt severe counts; HIT: anti-PF4/heparin IgG activates platelets, producing thrombosis
**Kasabach-Merritt**: infant vascular tumor (kaposiform hemangioendothelioma/tufted angioma; older exams: hemangioma) traps platelets → severe thrombocytopenia, consumptive coagulopathy

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Repeat CBC + peripheral smear**; platelet clumps → citrate tube for pseudothrombocytopenia
Isolated low platelets, normal coagulation, large platelets → ITP after excluding secondary causes
Schistocytes → LDH, haptoglobin, creatinine, coagulation studies; suspected TTP → urgent ADAMTS13 sample
HIV/HCV testing for new ITP; marrow biopsy only atypical cytopenias or suspected marrow disease
4Ts estimates HIT probability; intermediate/high → PF4 immunoassay, functional confirmation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Adult ITP **<30,000/µL or bleeding → glucocorticoid**; children without significant bleeding → observation
★ ITP critical bleeding → **IVIG + high-dose steroid + platelet transfusion**
Drug immune thrombocytopenia → stop culprit; persistent ITP → rituximab, thrombopoietin agonist, or selected splenectomy
Suspected TTP → plasma exchange; HIT → stop heparin, start argatroban/nonheparin anticoagulant
Older board LP target: 50,000/µL; current trigger below; neurosurgical targets often ≥100,000/µL

rows.label: Complications
items: Intracranial hemorrhage with severe disease; thrombosis in HIT/TTP
Steroid toxicity, immunosuppression; splenectomy → encapsulated bacterial sepsis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid culprit rechallenge, aspirin/NSAIDs when bleeding risk high; vaccinate before splenectomy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Von Willebrand disease: often normal platelet count with mucocutaneous bleeding
Marrow failure: additional cytopenias, abnormal precursor morphology

thrombocytopenia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AABB/ICTMG platelet recommendations (2025)](https://www.aabb.org/news-resources/news/article/2025/05/29/aabb-develops-new-platelet-transfusion-guidelines); other hematology principles not separately checked.

thrombotic-microangiopathies.name: Thrombotic microangiopathies
thrombotic-microangiopathies.scope: Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (ADAMTS13, pentad, plasma exchange), hemolytic uremic syndrome (shiga toxin, supportive care), atypical HUS, schistocytes, MAHA
thrombotic-microangiopathies.core: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia plus thrombocytopenia and organ injury: urgently distinguish TTP, Shiga toxin-associated HUS, and complement-mediated HUS.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immune TTP: acquired ADAMTS13 autoantibody; autoimmune disease, pregnancy, HIV can trigger episodes
STEC-HUS: contaminated food/water, often children; recurrent episodes suggest inherited complement susceptibility
Secondary TMA: severe hypertension, pregnancy complications, transplant, calcineurin inhibitors or other drugs

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Schistocytes**, ↑LDH/indirect bilirubin, ↓haptoglobin, reticulocytosis; direct antiglobulin test usually negative
TTP often neurologic/cardiac-predominant; HUS often renal-predominant, with substantial overlap
Classical TTP pentad: hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, fever, neurologic changes, renal dysfunction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Platelet-rich microthrombi shear passing erythrocytes and obstruct small-vessel perfusion

rows.label: Dx
items: CBC/smear, hemolysis studies, creatinine, urinalysis, PT/aPTT/fibrinogen; coagulation usually normal unlike DIC
★ **High PLASMIC score** supports empiric TTP management while awaiting definitive testing
ECG/troponin and neurologic examination assess otherwise occult organ injury
Normal complement levels do not exclude atypical HUS

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Suspected immune TTP → **treat immediately**; do not await full pentad or confirmatory result
★ STEC disease: **avoid antibiotics/antimotility drugs**; RBC transfusion for symptomatic anemia
TTP: no platelets unless life-threatening bleeding; plasma infusion only if exchange unavoidably delayed

rows.label: Complications
items: Stroke, myocardial ischemia, seizures, renal failure, death; survivors may develop CKD or cognitive impairment
Caplacizumab → bleeding; complement inhibition → meningococcal infection

rows.label: Prevention
items: TTP remission → monitor ADAMTS13/relapse symptoms; treat marked recurrent deficiency with hematology
★ Before complement blockade: **MenACWY + MenB**; urgent start before vaccine protection → penicillin prophylaxis
Food safety and hand hygiene reduce STEC exposure

rows.label: Mimics
items: DIC: prolonged clotting times, low fibrinogen, systemic coagulation activation
HELLP: pregnancy-associated hypertension, elevated liver enzymes; delivery central to treatment
B12 deficiency: macrocytosis, low reticulocyte response despite striking LDH

table.title: Decisive subtype branches
rows: Urgent plasma exchange + steroids, caplacizumab, rituximab
Shiga injury; often after bloody diarrhea

type-2-diabetes-mellitus.name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Diagnosis, glycemic targets, pharmacotherapy (metformin contraindications, SGLT2i, GLP-1 RA, insulin), chronic complications screening, pediatric screening in obesity
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.core: Insulin resistance with progressive beta-cell failure produces chronic hyperglycemia and vascular injury, often preceding obvious symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Central obesity, family history, prior gestational diabetes, PCOS, physical inactivity
Glucocorticoids and atypical antipsychotics can unmask dysglycemia

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, recurrent candidiasis; acanthosis nigricans suggests marked insulin resistance
Weight loss, ketosis, or dehydration → severe insulin deficiency; reconsider diabetes type

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired glucose uptake + excess hepatic output; early compensatory **↑serum insulin**, later relative secretory failure

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **A1c ≥6.5%**, fasting glucose ≥126, or 2-hour OGTT ≥200 mg/dL
Random glucose ≥200 with classic symptoms also diagnostic; otherwise confirm with second abnormal result
A1c unreliable with altered erythrocyte survival; use plasma glucose
★ Youth: screen puberty/age 10, whichever earlier, with overweight/obesity + additional risk; repeat ≥every 2 years

rows.label: Tx
items: Lifestyle + metformin; **lactic acidosis**: avoid eGFR <30, AKI/sepsis, hypoxia; no new start <45; reduce 30–44
★ HF/CKD → **SGLT2 inhibitor**; ASCVD/obesity → GLP-1 RA, independent of A1c or metformin
★ Catabolism, glucose ≥300, or A1c >10% → **insulin**
Otherwise GLP-1 RA before insulin; older exam questions may expect **basal insulin** once two orals fail
Adults: A1c <7%, fasting 80–130, postmeal <180; relax for frailty/hypoglycemia; quarterly checks until stable

rows.label: Complications
items: Retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, foot ulceration; coronary, cerebral, and peripheral arterial disease
SGLT2 inhibitors: genital mycoses, euglycemic DKA; sulfonylureas/insulin: hypoglycemia, weight gain
Metformin: GI intolerance, B12 deficiency; pioglitazone: edema, HF; sulfonylureas: labeled caution with sulfa allergy

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ At diagnosis then annually: **urine albumin/creatinine, eGFR, foot and dilated eye examinations** (eye spacing by findings)
★ Albuminuria + hypertension → **ACE inhibitor/ARB**, never both; efferent dilation ↓intraglomerular pressure
BP ≥130/80 → antihypertensive; older exam questions may expect ACE inhibitor, also normotensive albuminuria
Statin age 40–75; glycemic control slows **neuropathy**, retinopathy, nephropathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Type 1 diabetes: autoantibodies, low C-peptide, abrupt ketosis
Diabetes insipidus: dilute polyuria without elevated blood glucose

urinary-incontinence.name: Urinary incontinence
urinary-incontinence.core: Involuntary urine leakage is classified by triggers, urgency, bladder emptying, and ability to reach a toilet; reversible contributors often coexist.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Childbirth, pelvic surgery, aging, obesity; diabetes, neurologic disease, prostate enlargement
Diuretics, sedatives, anticholinergics, constipation, infection, impaired mobility/cognition worsen control

rows.label: Clues
items: History: timing, volume, dysuria, weak stream, nocturia, fluid intake, obstetric/surgical and neurologic history
★ **New saddle anesthesia, leg weakness, retention** → urgent cauda equina evaluation
Continuous leakage after pelvic surgery/radiation suggests fistula; recurrent UTIs/hematuria require further investigation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stress: aging/multiparity weaken pelvic floor → **urethral hypermobility**, low sphincter tone
Urge: **uninhibited detrusor contractions** (detrusor instability), worsened by caffeine; MS lesion → low residual
Overflow: **detrusor underactivity/acontractile bladder** (MS, diabetes, stroke) or outlet obstruction → high residual
Functional impairment can prevent continence despite intact lower urinary tract function

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis + voiding diary**, focused pelvic/prostate and neurologic examination; review medications
Cough stress test with reasonably full bladder; assess prolapse, atrophy, fecal impaction
**Q-tip excursion >30°** on Valsalva → urethral hypermobility (urethrocele)
★ Suspected retention/emptying symptoms → **postvoid residual**; persistent >200 mL suggests inadequate emptying
No routine initial urodynamics/cystoscopy; uncertainty, hematuria, refractory symptoms → additional testing

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat reversible contributor; mixed incontinence → target most bothersome component
★ **Pelvic floor training/bladder training** underpin conservative care; weight loss, reduce caffeine, timed voiding
Urgency drugs: mirabegron or antimuscarinic (oxybutynin); discuss cognitive risk and avoid antimuscarinics with retention
Mirabegron may increase BP; avoid severe uncontrolled hypertension; refractory urgency → botulinum toxin or neuromodulation
Genitourinary syndrome of menopause → local vaginal estrogen when suitable; not systemic estrogen for leakage

rows.label: Complications
items: Dermatitis, falls from rushing, social isolation, sleep disruption
Overflow → hydronephrosis/renal injury; bladder botulinum toxin → retention, UTI

rows.label: Prevention
items: Medication review, accessible toilet, mobility aids; bowel regularity, maintain strength and weight

rows.label: Mimics
items: Polyuria: high urine volume from hyperglycemia/diuresis rather than primary storage failure
Vaginal fistula: constant leakage unrelated to voiding urge or exertion

urinary-tract-infections.name: Urinary tract infections
urinary-tract-infections.scope: Asymptomatic bacteriuria, acute cystitis, pyelonephritis, catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI), catheter removal, empiric antibiotics
urinary-tract-infections.core: Symptoms localize urinary infection: bladder disease lacks systemic illness; renal involvement causes fever or flank pain; bacteriuria alone is insufficient.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual activity, spermicides, pregnancy, obstruction/stones, urinary retention, instrumentation
Catheter duration, diabetes, prior resistant isolates or antibiotics increase complicated-course risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic discomfort; absent vaginal discharge supports urinary source
★ **Rigors, CVA tenderness, vomiting, hypotension** → pyelonephritis or urosepsis
Catheterized patients: new urinary/systemic symptoms; cloudy urine or pyuria alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Usually ascending enteric bacteria, predominantly E coli; catheter biofilm maintains colonization
Urease-producing Proteus alkalinizes urine → struvite calculi and persistent infection
Pregnancy: progesterone ureteral relaxation + uterine compression → **stasis**; physiologic right-sided ureteral dilation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**: pyuria, leukocyte esterase, nitrites; pyelonephritis → heavy pyuria, WBC clumps/casts; negative nitrites don't exclude
Culture: pyelonephritis, pregnancy, CAUTI, recurrence/resistance; classic cystitis often clinical
Persistent fever after 48–72 hours, sepsis, or suspected obstruction → renal imaging
Asymptomatic bacteriuria: usually ≥100,000 CFU/mL; delirium alone → seek other causes without automatic antibiotics
Febrile non-toilet-trained child → **catheterized** urinalysis/culture; bag/clean-catch contaminate

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat asymptomatic bacteriuria only in pregnancy or before urologic mucosal trauma** in routine adult scenarios
★ CAUTI → **remove unnecessary catheter**; if needed and present >2 weeks, replace before culture/treatment
★ Infected obstructed collecting system → **urgent drainage + IV antibiotics**; antibiotics alone insufficient
Improving nonpregnant pyelonephritis: fluoroquinolone 5–7 days, other active drugs 7 days; high-risk cases individualized
Febrile infant → **cefotaxime/ceftriaxone**; first-generation cefazolin inadequate

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, septic shock, renal/perinephric abscess; pregnancy → preterm birth
Antibiotics → resistance, C difficile; fluoroquinolones → tendon injury, QT prolongation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid unnecessary catheters; closed drainage, daily removal assessment
Postmenopausal recurrence → vaginal estrogen
Recurrence ≥3/year or ≥2 in 6 months → postcoital or daily nitrofurantoin/TMP-SMX
Sporadic postcoital cystitis → **void before/after intercourse**; stop diaphragm/spermicide; condoms don't prevent

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vaginitis: discharge, pruritus, external burning
Urethritis: sexual exposure, discharge, positive gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT
Bladder pain syndrome: chronic symptoms, repeatedly negative cultures

table.title: Initial antibiotics; tailor to culture/resistance
rows: Ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin; initial ceftriaxone if resistance risk
IV fluids + ceftriaxone; cefepime/piperacillin-tazobactam if Pseudomonas risk
Avoid nitrofurantoin/fosfomycin: inadequate renal tissue levels

vaginitis.name: Vaginitis
vaginitis.scope: Bacterial vaginosis, Trichomoniasis, Vulvovaginal candidiasis, atrophic vaginitis, genitourinary syndrome of menopause
vaginitis.core: Vaginal discharge or irritation requires distinction among dysbiosis, sexually transmitted protozoal infection, yeast overgrowth, and hypoestrogenic mucosal change.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: BV: new partners, douching; trichomoniasis: sexual exposure
Candida: antibiotics, pregnancy, diabetes, immunosuppression; atrophy: menopause or other hypoestrogenic states
Prepubertal: hand inoculation of respiratory pathogens during URI

rows.label: Clues
items: Pruritus, dysuria, dyspareunia; discharge appearance overlaps, so symptoms alone insufficient
★ **Fever, lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness** → evaluate PID rather than isolated vaginitis
Postmenopausal bleeding needs assessment beyond assuming atrophy
★ Prepubertal **foul purulent/bloody discharge** → retained vaginal **foreign body**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: BV: lactobacilli depleted, anaerobes expand; Candida causes inflammatory overgrowth
Low estrogen thins epithelium and reduces lactobacilli → mucosal fragility and elevated vaginal pH

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Vaginal pH, saline/KOH microscopy**, history and examination; NAAT improves infectious diagnosis
BV: ≥3 Amsel—discharge, ↑pH, clue cells, amine odor; Gardnerella culture unhelpful (normal flora)
★ Suspected trichomoniasis + negative wet mount → **NAAT**, not reassurance
Recurrent/complicated Candida → culture or PCR for species; asymptomatic colonization alone needs no treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **oral metronidazole 7 days in women**; treat partners, abstain until completed/resolved
BV → oral metronidazole 7 days or vaginal metronidazole/clindamycin, **no routine partner treatment**, ACOG: treat if recurrent; treat symptomatic pregnancy
Candida → topical azole/nystatin or oral fluconazole; **pregnancy: topical azole 7 days**, avoid oral fluconazole
GSM → moisturizers/lubricants, then low-dose vaginal estrogen for persistent symptoms
Recurrent BV: ACOG 2025 considers male-partner metronidazole + topical clindamycin; older boards omit

rows.label: Complications
items: BV/trichomoniasis associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes and increased STI acquisition
Recurrent symptoms → reassess diagnosis, adherence, reinfection, diabetes or resistant/non-albicans yeast

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Trichomoniasis → **retest women at about 3 months**; condoms
Avoid douching/irritants; no routine partner treatment for uncomplicated Candida

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cervicitis: endocervical mucopus, friability, positive GC/CT NAAT
Contact dermatitis: external irritation after product exposure
Sarcoma botryoides: girl with bleeding, grape-like polypoid vaginal mass

valvular-heart-disease.name: Valvular heart disease
valvular-heart-disease.scope: Aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation, mitral stenosis, mitral regurgitation, mitral valve prolapse, physical exam, echocardiography, surgical and transcatheter replacement
valvular-heart-disease.core: Murmur timing, location, radiation, and loading maneuvers localize valve disease; symptoms and ventricular response determine intervention.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Trileaflet calcification, age >70 → AS; rheumatic disease → MS
Bicuspid valve: murmur from youth, premature calcific AS (40s–60s); childhood **endocarditis**; adult aortic dissection
AR: endocarditis, dissection, **root dilation** (Marfan, hypertension; murmur along right sternal border)
MR: ischemia, myxomatous prolapse (connective tissue laxity), chamber dilation

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, pulmonary edema, reduced exercise tolerance; abrupt deterioration suggests acute regurgitation
★ **Exertional syncope, angina, or HF** with obstruction → severe symptomatic disease
Squatting/handgrip increase regurgitant murmurs; standing/Valsalva → earlier MVP click, squatting → later

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stenosis produces upstream pressure overload; regurgitation produces chamber volume overload
Acute regurgitation lacks compensatory dilation, rapidly elevating filling pressures and reducing forward output
Mitral stenosis: ↑LA pressure, ↑PCWP, ↑pulmonary artery pressure; **LVEDP normal**; AF abolishes presystolic accentuation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TTE Doppler** defines anatomy, severity, EF, chamber dimensions, pulmonary pressures
Severe AS: velocity ≥4 m/s, mean gradient ≥40, or valve area ≤1 cm²; discordance requires reassessment
Severe MS: valve area ≤1.5 cm²; TEE for thrombus before balloon intervention or uncertain anatomy
★ Acute murmur with shock → **urgent echocardiography**; TEE if endocarditis/dissection suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe AR/MR → **urgent surgery**, stabilize with afterload reduction/diuresis if BP permits
Severe primary MR: **EF ≤60% or LVESD ≥40 mm** triggers intervention even without symptoms
Secondary MR → optimize HF treatment first; selected persistent severe cases benefit from transcatheter edge-to-edge repair
Avoid excessive preload reduction in severe AS; symptomatic relief never replaces needed valve intervention

rows.label: Complications
items: Heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, AF, systemic embolism, endocarditis
Mechanical prosthesis: thrombosis/bleeding; bioprosthesis: structural degeneration
Prosthetic dysfunction/paravalvular leak → new murmur, **schistocytes**, hemolytic anemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Warfarin for mechanical valves**; no DOAC substitution; rheumatic MS with AF also requires warfarin
Prosthetic valve or prior endocarditis → selected dental prophylaxis; native isolated MVP does not qualify
Periodic echo and symptom review; treat rheumatic fever to prevent recurrent valve injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: HCM: systolic murmur increases with Valsalva/standing
Aortic sclerosis: ejection murmur without significant gradient; flow murmur: normal valve anatomy

table.title: Valve signatures and definitive options
rows: Crescendo-decrescendo, carotids; soft A2; pulsus parvus et tardus
Early diastolic decrescendo; wide pulse pressure
Loud S1, opening snap, apical mid-diastolic rumble
Suitable symptomatic rheumatic valve → balloon commissurotomy
LLSB holosystolic, louder on inspiration; right HF

valvular-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established echo thresholds and intervention framework.

venous-thromboembolism.name: Venous thromboembolism
venous-thromboembolism.core: Unilateral swollen leg or sudden unexplained dyspnea with pleuritic pain; pulmonary embolism severity determined by hemodynamics, not clot size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobilization, surgery, malignancy, estrogen, pregnancy/postpartum, inherited thrombophilia
**Previous VTE** is the strongest predictor of recurrence; remote surgery months ago adds little
**Central venous catheter** → main cause of upper-extremity DVT

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT: asymmetric calf tenderness, warmth; PE: tachycardia, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, sometimes normal oxygen saturation
Syncope, elevated JVP, cool extremities → impending RV failure; normal chest radiograph does not exclude PE

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis/endothelial injury/hypercoagulability → venous clot; pulmonary obstruction → V/Q mismatch, RV pressure overload
Massive PE: high RA/PA pressure, low PCWP, low output; RV infarct: PA pressure normal/low

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Wells/pretest probability** first; very low-risk + PERC-negative → no testing
★ Low/intermediate probability → **D-dimer**; negative excludes; positive/high probability → **CT pulmonary angiography**
Age >50: D-dimer threshold age × 10 ng/mL FEU; contrast contraindication → V/Q scan
DVT → compression US; negative proximal scan + persistent suspicion → repeat in 1 week
Low-probability V/Q + high clinical suspicion is nondiagnostic → **CT angiography**

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Oxygen/support circulation; unstable and unsafe for CT → bedside **echo**; high suspicion/delayed imaging → anticoagulate
★ Stable VTE → **apixaban/rivaroxaban**; cancer → LMWH/DOAC; pregnancy → LMWH; severe renal failure → UFH
Lysis contraindicated/fails → catheter thrombectomy/surgical embolectomy; active intracranial bleeding precludes lysis
Acute proximal DVT/PE + absolute anticoagulation contraindication → temporary **IVC filter**, remove when feasible
Acute proximal DVT/PE without DOAC → immediate **heparin**; warfarin alone never initial; inferior in cancer

rows.label: Complications
items: Postthrombotic syndrome; persistent dyspnea → evaluate chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis → bleeding; heparin → HIT

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Major transient trigger → **3 months** anticoagulation; unprovoked/persistent risk → extended course if low bleeding risk
Aspirin or 1 month inadequate; DOACs now preferred, older exam questions may expect warfarin 3–6 months
Hospital prophylaxis: LMWH; active bleeding → intermittent pneumatic compression; early mobilization
Hip arthroplasty → LMWH, warfarin or DOAC; aspirin now accepted, older exam questions may expect anticoagulant

rows.label: Mimics
items: Cellulitis: predominantly skin erythema, portal of entry
Ruptured Baker cyst: posterior knee symptoms, cyst on US
Pneumonia: focal infiltrate and infectious prodrome
Amniotic fluid embolism: peripartum collapse with **DIC/low fibrinogen**

table.title: Treatment branches; 2026 PE guidance uses categories A–E
rows: Stable; low PESI/sPESI; no RV injury
Normotensive + RV dysfunction and/or troponin elevation
Sustained SBP <90 mm Hg or shock

vertigo.name: Vertigo
vertigo.scope: Peripheral vs central vertigo, benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (Dix-Hallpike, Epley maneuver), vestibular neuritis and labyrinthitis, Meniere disease, vestibular migraine
vertigo.core: Illusion of movement: timing, triggers, hearing findings and neurologic examination distinguish benign vestibular disease from posterior-circulation ischemia.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older age, vascular risk factors → central ischemia; recent viral illness, head injury or migraine history
Ototoxic drugs and ear disease can cause peripheral vestibular injury

rows.label: Clues
items: Peripheral: horizontal-torsional unidirectional nystagmus, reduced with fixation; no focal neurologic deficit
★ **Vertical/direction-changing nystagmus, skew deviation, severe truncal ataxia or focal deficits** → central concern
New unilateral hearing loss with continuous acute vertigo can represent AICA stroke, not simply labyrinthitis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Asymmetric vestibular input → movement illusion and nystagmus; central lesions involve brainstem/cerebellum
BPPV: displaced **otoliths (canaliths)** in semicircular canal → position-triggered endolymph movement

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Dix-Hallpike** for triggered episodic symptoms; typical upbeat torsional nystagmus has latency and fatigues
Continuous acute syndrome with spontaneous nystagmus → **HINTS by trained clinician**; not for brief positional episodes
★ Normal head impulse, direction-changing nystagmus or skew → **stroke evaluation/MRI ± CTA/MRA**
Untrained examiner or concerning findings → MRI; early diffusion imaging may miss posterior stroke
Typical BPPV → no routine imaging; suspected Meniere → audiometry; horizontal positional nystagmus → supine-roll test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Central concern → urgent **stroke pathway**; negative head CT cannot exclude posterior infarction
Severe acute nausea → brief meclizine/ondansetron; prolonged vestibular suppressants impair compensation

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, dehydration, impaired driving; missed stroke → disability/death; recurrent inner-ear disease → hearing loss

rows.label: Prevention
items: Fall precautions, avoid driving during attacks; reduce individual migraine triggers and address vascular risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Orthostatic hypotension: standing-triggered presyncope with BP drop, rather than head-position-triggered nystagmus
Arrhythmia: episodic faintness/palpitations; ECG or monitoring establishes cardiac cause

table.title: Peripheral and episodic patterns
rows: Rehabilitation; discuss early steroids, benefit uncertain
